# TablePro Linux remediation plan: details

Companion to [plan-2026-09-14-audit-remediation.md](plan-2026-09-14-audit-remediation.md), which holds the landing sequence. This file holds the reviewed foundation designs, the reconciled contracts and every task specification.

## Foundations

### FA · Application, window and session ownership model

Foundation FA, revised after review. It replaces the global DatabaseService, the thread_local tracker registries, the flock gate and the RelmApp::run single-window root with this model:
- TableProApplication: an adw::Application GObject subclass (the Loupe/Fractal pattern). It owns app actions, GApplication uniqueness, a WindowRegistry of Controller<SessionWindow>, SessionRegistry, NetworkWatch and ResumeDetector.
- SessionWindow (one adw::ApplicationWindow per connection session) moves through picker, connecting and workspace pages. It owns ConnectAttempts, the close guard, the inhibitor and an explicit teardown order. Window actions live in the window's own GActionMap.
- Session is GTK-free and runtime-agnostic: Session::start needs no tokio context. Every task goes through an injected TaskSpawner (relm4 in production, a paused tokio Handle in tests). Operations lease a generation-stamped transport from a ConnectionLink through one OperationRunner chokepoint.
- An event-driven HealthMonitor runs a pure HealthPolicy over a coalescing MonitorMailbox:
  - Signals whose generation is not current are ignored.
  - Failed parks until the user retries.
  - Offline is decided per session from gio::NetworkMonitor::can_reach_future on the session's endpoint. Loopback and file endpoints are exempt.
- Driver changes that remove the Busy misclassification:
  - Connection::probe never waits on a pool slot or a client lock.
  - PoolTimedOut maps to Busy only when pool size equals max and no connection is idle.
- Teardown and quit are bounded:
  - Session::begin_shutdown cancels, takes the transport and closes it under a Close deadline, awaited under an ApplicationHoldGuard.
  - app.quit never calls g_application_quit. Windows close, and GApplication exits when the use count reaches zero.
- A save whose result is unknown freezes its tracker and is never resubmitted.
- The workspace store blocks writes after a failed load, and its directory is per profile.

Verified on disk:

#### Decisions

##### D1 · Application controller is a GObject subclass of adw::Application, not a RelmApp root

Add application/{mod,imp}.rs with TableProApplication. main.rs returns glib::ExitCode from app.run(), which implements Termination.

Vfuncs:
- startup: parent startup, install app actions and accels, start HistoryService, NetworkWatch, and the ResumeDetector lifecycle subscription.
- activate: present active_window(), or open a picker window.
- open(files): one WindowLaunch::OpenFile per file.
- handle_local_options:
  - Without --new-window: Continue(()).
  - With it: register(None). On Err, log and Break(ExitCode::FAILURE). If is_remote(), activate_action("new-window", None) and Break(ExitCode::SUCCESS). Otherwise (primary) Continue(()), so the default activate opens exactly one window.
- shutdown: clear the WindowRegistry.

Windows are Components started with Component::builder(). The root is added with app.add_window before launch, the controller goes into WindowRegistry, and it is removed in connect_window_removed.

Because RelmApp::run is bypassed, relm4's RUNTIME is never entered on the GTK thread. So:
- All tokio-context work (time, IO, Handle::current, as in the MSSQL connect) runs inside futures spawned through TaskSpawner (D15) or GuardedCommand.
- GTK-thread code only builds runtime-free primitives: watch, Notify, CancellationToken, async_channel.

crates/app/clippy.toml bans relm4::RelmApp::run, relm4::main_application, relm4::main_adw_application, relm4::actions::RelmActionGroup::register_for_main_application, relm4::ComponentBuilder::transient_for and relm4::ComponentBuilder::transient_for_native.

**Why**: RelmApp::run ties the app to one root window and activates with set_visible(true). It offers no open or handle-local-options hook, and it holds RUNTIME.enter() plus shutdown_all, which are useful only to RelmApp roots.

The review is correct that skipping RUNTIME.enter() makes a GTK-thread tokio::time or Handle::current call panic. That is why tokio-context work is confined to spawned futures and Session::start is specified runtime-free, with a #[gtk::test] that proves it.

The primary-instance branch fixes a defect in the previous design: a primary started with --new-window returned Break and exited right after startup.

**Rejected**: - RelmApp::from_app(app).run::<WelcomeWindow>: the welcome root outlives or hides behind session windows.
- Entering relm4's runtime by blocking on a spawned Handle::current(): a startup hack that hides context bugs instead of removing them.
- Keeping single_instance.rs: it blocks activate forwarding (F-068).

##### D2 · One window per session: picker -> connecting -> workspace; disconnect returns to picker

Every adw::ApplicationWindow is a SessionWindow on one of three pages:
- Picker: WelcomeView.
- Connecting / ConnectFailed: an adw::StatusPage with an adw::Spinner. Cancel is bound to win.cancel-connect; Retry and Edit Connection appear after a failure.
- Workspace: a child Workspace component.

app.new-window (<Primary><Shift>n, the GNOME Console precedent) opens a picker window. Every connect path claims a SessionKey before any network work (D16). If another window holds the key, that window is presented.

win.disconnect runs the ordered teardown in D17 and shows the picker again.

**Why**: This follows the owner's window-per-connection decision and the Text Editor/Console New Window model. A Workspace never changes session, so no retargeting path exists (F-002).

**Rejected**: - Closing the window on disconnect plus a separate welcome window.
- Swapping sessions inside one Workspace with generation stamps.
- Opening the window only after connect succeeds: Cancel and Retry would then have no owner.

##### D3 · Session: generation-stamped leases, OperationRunner chokepoint, runtime-free start, bounded shutdown

Session holds:
- metadata, read_only, endpoint.
- runner: OperationRunner, which is Clone and 'static: Arc<ConnectionLink>, Arc<dyn DeadlinePolicy>, Arc<MonitorMailbox>, a health watch::Receiver and a CancellationToken.
- catalog: Arc<SchemaCatalog>.
- spawner: Arc<dyn TaskSpawner>.
- _cancel_on_drop: tokio_util::sync::DropGuard.
- _monitor: tokio_util::task::AbortOnDropHandle<()>. crates/app enables tokio-util feature rt.

Session::start(pending, SessionDeps { connector, credentials, deadlines, spawner }) builds only runtime-free primitives and spawns run_monitor through the spawner, so it is safe on the GTK thread.

ConnectionLink wraps watch::Sender<LinkState { generation: LinkGeneration, transport: Option<Arc<Transport>> }>.
- lease() returns ConnectionLease { generation, transport }.
- replace() bumps the generation and returns a RetiredTransport.
- take() empties the link.

Retired transports close immediately. RetiredTransport::close(deadline) awaits Connection::close(&self) under tokio::time::timeout. Ok reports Closed, Err reports CloseFailed, and a timeout reports Abandoned (the close future is dropped). The Arc<Transport>, and so the SSH tunnel, is freed when the last lease drops. Each lease holder is already bounded by its own operation deadline.

Session::begin_shutdown(&self) -> TaskResult<CloseReport> does three things synchronously:
1. Cancels the token, so every run() returns Closed and drops its lease.
2. Takes the transport.
3. Spawns RetiredTransport::close(deadlines.deadline(OperationKind::Close)), with a 5 s default.
It is idempotent: a second call yields AlreadyClosed. The GTK side awaits the TaskResult while holding app.hold().

Drop only cancels (DropGuard) and aborts the monitor (AbortOnDropHandle).

core Connection::close becomes &self and idempotent.

**Why**: Review: loss signals carried no generation, so a closed old transport kept re-triggering reconnects. Leases and signals are now stamped, and the policy ignores stale generations.

Review: 'closed once its last lease ends' had no mechanism. The replaced transport has been declared lost or suspect, so closing it immediately under a deadline is correct and needs no Drop-time await.

Review: shutdown had no deadline. The Close deadline bounds sqlx Pool::close, which waits for checked-out connections, and the MSSQL mutex. Cancelling first releases leases, so the close usually finishes well inside the deadline.

Review: the signatures were inconsistent. They are unified around OperationRunner and SessionDeps.

**Rejected**: - Closing a replaced transport when its last lease drops: Drop cannot await, and a lease stuck in a hung operation would pin the tunnel with no bound.
- RwLock<Arc<dyn Connection>>: no generation, no notification.
- Close inside Drop via a detached spawn: no hold guard, and it races exit.
- Mutex<Option<JoinHandle>> plus a manual Drop: AbortOnDropHandle and DropGuard say the same thing declaratively.

##### D4 · Connect attempts: per-window generation gate, cancellation, adoption only on the GTK thread

ConnectAttempts (pure, !Send, one per SessionWindow):
- begin() bumps AttemptGeneration, cancels the previous token and returns AttemptTicket.
- The GuardedCommand future:
  1. Resolves the ConnectSource into a ConnectRequest. A Saved source is re-read from storage, with secrets loaded from the keyring; errors propagate.
  2. Runs Connector::establish(request, ticket.cancel) with ConnectDeadlines { ssh_handshake 15 s, driver_connect 20 s, initial_catalog 15 s, close 5 s }.
  3. Returns AttemptOutcome.
- On the GTK thread: if attempts.accepts(generation) and the page is still Connecting for the same claim, adopt with Session::start(pending, services.session_deps(key)) and claim.attach(&session). Then persist a pending ConnectDialog save, spawn touch_last_opened and launch the Workspace.
- Otherwise spawner.spawn(pending.discard()), which closes the connection under the close deadline and drops its tunnel.

establish selects on cancel between stages. A stage that completes after cancel closes its own objects before returning Cancelled.

**Why**: This is the Rust twin of the macOS ConnectionAttemptRegistry invariant: cancelling does not stop the driver, and a late attempt never clobbers the winner. The MSSQL blocking GSSAPI login keeps running on the blocking pool and drops its own client.

**Rejected**: - Adopting inside the async task.
- A global attempt registry.
- Aborting the JoinHandle only.

##### D5 · Health: pure HealthPolicy over a coalescing mailbox; probe outside the pool; Failed parks; per-session reachability

run_monitor loop, in tokio::select! (biased) order:
1. cancel.cancelled()
2. mailbox.next()
3. sleep_until(policy.next_deadline()), or pending when parked.

MonitorMailbox is a std Mutex<PendingSignals> plus tokio::sync::Notify. post() merges signals (max generation per kind, latest reachability, longest resume) and never drops one, so RetryNow cannot be lost.

Probe: Connection::probe under deadlines.deadline(Probe), 10 s by default. ProbeOutcome::classify returns:
- Healthy.
- Busy (DriverError::Busy from a server that refuses new sessions).
- Unresponsive (timeout, or Query/Internal errors).
- Lost (is_connection_lost).
- Rejected(FailureCause) (AuthFailed, Tls, IntegratedAuth).

Policy by state:
- Online:
  - Probes every 30 s. Healthy and Busy stay Online and reset failures.
  - Unresponsive counts toward LOST_AFTER_FAILURES = 3, re-probing after 10 s.
  - Lost moves to Reconnecting { attempt 1 } with an immediate Reconnect, or to Offline when the endpoint is Unreachable.
  - Rejected on a probe stays Online with a warning: the live transport is still authenticated, and only a new login was refused.
  - OperationPanicked { current generation } or Resumed triggers an immediate Probe.
- Reconnecting:
  - Backoff 5 s doubling to 60 s.
  - Connected(generation) moves to Online and adopts the generation.
  - A reconnect Rejected(cause) moves to Failed { cause } and Park.
  - Unreachable moves to Offline.
- Offline:
  - No backoff escalation. One Reconnect every 60 s (OFFLINE_RECHECK), so false negatives and captive portals self-heal.
  - Reachable, Resumed or RetryNow moves to Reconnecting { attempt 1 } with an immediate Reconnect.
- Failed (parked):
  - No timers. Only RetryNow reconnects; Reachability and Resumed never unpark.
  - Only the cancel token ends the task.
- Any state:
  - ConnectionLost, OperationPanicked and OperationSucceeded whose generation is not policy.generation() are ignored.
  - OperationSucceeded { current } moves Reconnecting or Offline to Online, because sqlx pools heal dead connections themselves.

On a successful reconnect the monitor:
- replaces the link,
- spawns the retired close,
- commits the PendingSession tables to SchemaCatalog (fetch-first, commit-over),
- builds the request from ReconnectPlan { connector, request, credentials }. CredentialSource::refresh re-reads only secrets from the keyring, so a user who fixes a password or runs kinit and clicks Retry succeeds, and host, database and user never change (no retarget).

Reachability:
- NetworkEndpoint::for_request gives Remote { ssh bastion host:port, or service host:port }, or Local for file-based drivers, loopback IPs, 'localhost', '.', and unix-socket paths.
- NetworkWatch (GTK thread) listens to network-changed and notify::connectivity. ReachabilityFanout evaluates each attached Remote session through ReachabilityProbe (production: gio::NetworkMonitor::default().can_reach_future(&gio::NetworkAddress::new(host, port))), stamped so only the latest result is delivered, as MonitorSignal::Reachability.
- Local sessions are never gated.

ResumeDetector: a CLOCK_BOOTTIME vs CLOCK_MONOTONIC drift above 2 s on a 5 s tick. It runs through the spawner only while SessionRegistry::live_count() > 0, driven by claim attach and release events.

The banner Retry button uses action-name win.reconnect, which posts RetryNow.

**Why**: Review: PoolTimedOut is ambiguous (verified in inner.rs, where connect retries until the deadline). The probe therefore no longer uses the pool acquire path (C6), and operation errors classify pool pressure from pool state.

On the review's suggested test 'four long queries plus a probe yield Busy': with an out-of-pool probe, a saturated pool on a live server makes the probe Healthy and a user operation Busy. That is the intended split: user operations report Busy, the probe proves liveness. The testcontainers tests assert exactly that.

Review: Stop broke Retry. Park keeps the mailbox alive.

Review: network-available is a default-route flag (GIO docs recommend can_reach per host). Reachability is now per session with loopback and file exemptions, and a successful operation clears Offline.

notify::connectivity is kept alongside network-changed because portal to full transitions do not always change routes.

**Rejected**: - A bounded mpsc with try_send: drops RetryNow under load.
- Global network-available gating: false Offline for loopback, LAN and VPN.
- logind PrepareForSleep: needs a Flathub system-bus exception.
- Re-running resolve_saved on reconnect: silently retargets a live session after the user edits host settings.
- 1 Hz polling.

##### D6 · Per-workspace tracker registries with borrow-safe handles

Delete the thread_local REGISTRY and the free functions in change_tracker.rs and structure_tracker.rs.

Workspace owns Rc<ChangeTrackerRegistry> and Rc<StructureTrackerRegistry>. They hand out TabTrackerHandle and StructureTrackerHandle, which are newtypes over Rc<RefCell<..>>.

Handle rules:
- The RefCell never leaves the handle.
- Every method borrows only for its own body, calls no GTK and no callbacks, and returns owned data (CellOverlay, RowState, TrackerDelta, PendingSummary, SaveBatch).
- Grid code applies a TrackerDelta to its gio::ListStore after the call returns.
- Change notifications go through the existing relm4 channel forward, never through synchronous callbacks.
- No try_borrow fallback exists.

Workspace::dirty_tabs() aggregates both registries and feeds WorkspaceOutput::DirtyChanged.

**Why**: F-076: global registries leak edits across windows.

Review: the try_borrow fallback rendered stale data. Owned snapshots make a re-entrant borrow structurally impossible, so no fallback is needed.

**Rejected**: - A thread_local keyed by (window, tab).
- Arc<Mutex> trackers.
- try_borrow with a raw-value fallback: shows the database value instead of the pending edit.

##### D7 · Panic boundary at the command and spawn layers plus a process hook

- catch_panic(fut) = futures::FutureExt::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(fut)) mapped to TaskPanic.
- GuardedCommand on ComponentSender<C> offers guarded_command (drop_on_shutdown) and guarded_command_detached. Both always deliver Result<T, TaskPanic>.
- TaskSpawnerExt::spawn_task and spawn_blocking_task wrap work in catch_panic and deliver TaskResult<T>, which resolves to Result<T, TaskFailure::{Panicked, Aborted}>.
- install_panic_hook() logs through tracing::error!(target: "panic") with location, thread and message.
- panic="unwind" in every profile.

crates/app/clippy.toml (nearest-file lookup; msrv repeated) bans:
- relm4::ComponentSender::{command, spawn_command, oneshot_command, spawn_oneshot_command} (allowed only in runtime/command_boundary.rs)
- relm4::spawn and relm4::spawn_blocking (allowed only in runtime/relm4_spawner.rs)
- tokio::spawn, tokio::task::spawn_blocking, tokio::runtime::Handle::spawn and tokio::runtime::Handle::spawn_blocking (allowed only in runtime/relm4_spawner.rs and the #[cfg(test)] test_support/tokio_spawner.rs)
- gio::prelude::ApplicationExt::quit
- the D1 relm4 application helpers

Driver and ssh crates keep the workspace clippy.toml.

**Why**: F-016: relm4 discards the JoinHandle.

Review: 'add_action with accelerators' cannot be expressed as a path, and the real stray-application paths were missing. Both are fixed, and the allow-list now matches the actual spawn sites, all routed through the spawner.

**Rejected**: - panic=abort.
- Awaiting a JoinHandle per command.
- Banning by argument shape: clippy matches paths only.

##### D8 · Tabs own their fetches through RequestSequencer; supersession includes a server-side cancel contract

BrowseTab and StructureTab become Components with their own CommandOutput.
- issue(kind) cancels the previous token of that kind and returns RequestTicket.
- Fetches call session.run_cancellable(kind, &ticket.cancel, op).
- Replies are Stamped and applied only if accept(kind, stamp).
- Closing a tab drops its component, its commands and its sequencer, and the sequencer cancels all tokens.
- The App messages FetchBrowse*, RowsLoaded, RowCountLoaded, ColumnsLoaded, TablesReloaded and StructureDataLoaded are deleted.

Cancellation contract for Page and Count: run_cancellable drops the operation future on cancel and returns OperationError::Cancelled. Per C6, dropping a fetch_rows or query future must also stop the statement on the server:
- PostgreSQL: pg_cancel_backend on the acquired backend pid.
- MySQL: KILL QUERY on CONNECTION_ID().
- ClickHouse: KILL QUERY by query_id.
- SQLite: sqlite3_interrupt through the sqlx lock_handle raw handle.
- MSSQL: tiberius has no attention API, so the dropped client is marked for replacement.

The driver implementations of that contract, with a conformance test per driver, belong to the network-loss workstream, the same workstream that owns keepalive and TCP_USER_TIMEOUT.

**Why**: F-040 and F-042. Review: client-side drop alone leaves server work running and can fill the 4-connection pool.

FA owns the chokepoint and the contract. Pool saturation can no longer hide liveness, because the probe is out of pool (D5). The server-side cancel is a driver capability implemented by the named workstream in the same plan.

**Rejected**: - Stamping inside App.
- A per-kind AbortHandle.
- A cancel method on Connection keyed by a request id: forces every driver to track ids even when cancel-on-drop expresses the same thing without a signature change.

##### D9 · SchemaCatalog in Session with shared in-flight fetches; a refresh never clears the cache

SchemaCatalog::new(initial, runner: OperationRunner, spawner) builds 'static fetch futures from the cloned runner and spawns them through the spawner wrapped in catch_panic. An awaiter that drops does not cancel a shared fetch.
- tables() joins in-flight work or returns the cache.
- refresh_tables() joins and sets rerun, so exactly one more fetch runs.
- A failure keeps the tables and sets last_error.
- columns(TableKey) uses the same pattern.
- invalidate_table marks the entry stale and keeps its data.
- commit_tables (reconnect) commits over the old value.
- The sidebar subscribes to the snapshot watch.

**Why**: F-133 and the invariants: schema loading awaits the shared task, and a refresh never clears the cache it is refreshing. Review: the fetch closure must be 'static, which OperationRunner makes possible.

**Rejected**: - A pending boolean.
- Per-tab list_tables calls.

##### D10 · Close, quit and logout are event-driven loops over SaveLedger and dialogs; quit exits by use count

SessionWindow connect_close_request returns Proceed only when close_approved is set. Otherwise it sends CloseRequested(CloseReason::Window) and returns Stop.

CloseGuard::run is an async loop on glib::spawn_future_local:
1. If saves are in flight: a waiting dialog (heading 'Saving Changes', single response 'cancel' labelled 'Keep Open') races choose_future against ledger.when_idle(). When idle, it force_close()s and loops.
2. If any dirty tab has PendingState::OutcomeUnknown: 'Save Result Unknown' dialog.
   - Body names the tabs: 'The connection was lost while saving. The changes may already be in the database.'
   - Responses: cancel 'Keep Open' (close response); reload 'Reload Table' (default; cancels the close, reloads those tabs and presents the first); discard 'Discard Changes' (destructive; clears the frozen sets and loops).
3. If other tabs are dirty: SaveChangesDialog, the Text Editor layout (AdwAlertDialog with an AdwPreferencesGroup of AdwActionRow plus GtkCheckButton). Responses are cancel, discard and save. Save saves the checked tabs, discards the unchecked ones and loops. A RolledBack save leaves its tracker dirty, so the loop re-prompts.
4. Otherwise Approved.

SaveOutcome::classify(Result<_, OperationError>):
- Ok: Committed.
- A known rollback (Transaction, Query, ReadOnly): RolledBack.
- A lost connection, TimedOut, Panicked, Closed, or a mid-batch failure on a driver without transactional DDL: Unknown(cause).

Unknown calls tracker.mark_outcome_unknown(). Frozen trackers return SaveRejection::OutcomeUnknown from begin_save, so their statements are never resubmitted.

QuitSequence (app.quit, <Primary>q):
- Loops over app.windows() not yet asked.
- For each: present it, send CloseRequested(Quit(oneshot)) and await. Any Cancelled aborts.
- Each approved window runs the D17 teardown and closes itself.
- The sequence never calls g_application_quit. GApplication leaves its loop when the use count reaches zero: after the last window is removed and the last teardown or save hold guard drops. Then shutdown runs.

WindowInhibitor: one cookie per window.
- LOGOUT with 'There are unsaved changes' while dirty.
- LOGOUT|SUSPEND with 'Saving changes' while saves are in flight.
- A cookie of 0 counts as not inhibited.

**Why**: F-036, F-067, F-110, F-019 routing.

Review: g_application_quit ignores the hold count (verified), which voided every hold guard. Exiting through the use count (verified in g_application_run) makes save tickets and session teardown real protections.

Review: Unknown re-prompted Save. On 'Refresh and Discard': a third 'Keep Open' response is kept so Escape never reloads or discards. Reload is the default, which gives the user the Refresh path.

**Rejected**: - A quit that calls app.quit() after approvals: kills commits and closes.
- One combined quit dialog.
- Resubmitting unknown saves: duplicate rows.
- Close Anyway with a background commit.

##### D11 · Runtime sizing and blocking I/O

configure_runtime_threads() runs first in main: RELM_THREADS = available_parallelism clamped to 2..=4.

- Delete the startup tokio runtime.
- HistoryService::start(retention_days, spawner) runs init plus prune through the spawner, keeps an hourly prune interval inside that task, and publishes watch<HistoryAvailability>. win.show-history is disabled until Ready.
- Config writes (column_widths, filter_settings, preferences, window_state) run through TaskSpawner::spawn_blocking with latest-wins coalescing.

**Why**: F-071.

**Rejected**: - A second app runtime.
- Unbounded worker count.

##### D12 · Workspace persistence: in memory, per SessionKey, off-thread writes, write-blocked after a failed load, per-profile directory

WorkspaceStore (GTK thread, Rc):
- Directory: AppPaths.state_dir.join("workspaces"), where state_dir = glib::user_state_dir().join(config::APP_ID). app.tablepro.TablePro and app.tablepro.TablePro.Devel never share files.
- File names: Saved(uuid) is <uuid>.json. File(uri) is file-<glib::compute_checksum_for_string(ChecksumType::Sha256, uri)>.json.
- load returns WorkspaceLoad::{Restored, Empty (NotFound), Blocked(WorkspaceLoadError)}.
- A Blocked key is recorded in the store. schedule and flush on it return WorkspaceSaveError::Blocked, and the file is never written.
- The Workspace shows one adw::Toast ('Saved tabs could not be read', button 'Reset' bound to win.reset-workspace-layout).
- reset renames the file to <name>.json.corrupt-<unix seconds> on the blocking pool and unblocks the key.

Writer task (through the spawner): keeps the latest record per key and writes with glib::file_set_contents_full(CONSISTENT|DURABLE, 0o600) on spawn_blocking. Flush replies through a oneshot.

PersistDebouncer::new(delay) is trailing; production uses 500 ms. SqlEditorOutput::ContentChanged carries no text.

Record version 1, with no migration: the app never shipped.

**Why**: F-070, F-002 persistence, F-105.

Review: the load-failure rule contradicted itself. Blocking by key with an explicit reset is unambiguous, and a newer-format file is never overwritten.

Review: the Devel profile collided with the stable one. The state dir is derived from APP_ID. In Flatpak, user_state_dir is already per app, and the joined id keeps one layout for host and sandbox.

**Rejected**: - A global JSON file.
- GSettings.
- Overwrite-on-next-change after a failed load (F-003 class).
- A shared state dir with a cross-profile lock.

##### D13 · GApplication uniqueness and launch surface

- Delete services/single_instance.rs.
- Flags: HANDLES_OPEN. resource-base-path: /app/tablepro/TablePro.
- Option: add_main_option("new-window", b'n', NONE, None, "Open a new window", None), handled as in D1.
- open: LaunchRequest::OpenFile resolves a SessionKey (D16), presents the owning window or opens a Connecting window.
- App actions: new-window <Primary><Shift>n, quit <Primary>q (QuitSequence), preferences <Primary>comma, about.
- shortcuts is auto-installed by AdwApplication from shortcuts-dialog.ui.
- Window actions are added to the adw::ApplicationWindow itself through ActionMapExtManual::add_action_entries, never through a separately inserted 'win' group. Workspace-scoped actions are added the same way and removed in Workspace::shutdown.
- The desktop file has DBusActivatable=true and Actions=new-window.
- config::APP_ID and the resource bundle come from D19.

**Why**: F-068.

Review: gtk_application_window_init already inserts 'win'. Verified in gtkapplicationwindow.c: a second group would replace the window's own map, which app accels and the D-Bus export (%s/window/%d) resolve through.

**Rejected**: - HANDLES_COMMAND_LINE.
- Ctrl+N for new-window.
- A gio::SimpleActionGroup inserted as 'win'.
- Keeping the flock.

##### D14 · Operation chokepoint with deadlines, generation observation and read replay

OperationRunner::run_cancellable(kind, cancel, op) is the only way UI code touches a connection; Session::run and run_cancellable delegate to it. It:
- leases the transport (returns Closed when there is none),
- selects on the session token and the caller token,
- applies DeadlinePolicy::deadline(kind),
- wraps the op in catch_panic.

Observation:
- is_connection_lost: posts ConnectionLost { lease generation }.
- TaskPanic: posts OperationPanicked { generation }.
- Success while health is not Online: posts OperationSucceeded { generation }.

Replay: when a replayable kind (Metadata, Page, Count) fails as lost and link.generation() is already newer than the lease, the op runs once more on the current lease. Query, Save and Close are never replayed. op is Fn(ConnectionLease) -> Fut.

OperationKind = { Metadata, Page, Count, Query { timeout }, Save, Probe, Close }. Defaults: Metadata 15 s, Page and Count 60 s, Query from the preference, Save 120 s, Probe 10 s, Close 5 s.

**Why**: F-002, F-072 and F-016 need one place. Review: generation stamping. Replay limited to idempotent reads keeps a tab from showing a spurious error right after a reconnect, without ever re-running writes.

**Rejected**: - Ad hoc session.connection() calls.
- Replaying every kind: duplicates DML.

##### D15 · Injected TaskSpawner for every background task

TaskSpawner (Send + Sync, object-safe):
- spawn(BoxFuture<'static, ()>) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>
- spawn_blocking(Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>) -> JoinHandle<()>

TaskSpawnerExt adds spawn_task and spawn_blocking_task, which return TaskResult<T> via a futures oneshot. TaskResult is awaitable from glib executors and detached, so dropping the awaiter does not abort.

Implementations:
- Production Relm4Spawner wraps relm4::spawn and relm4::spawn_blocking.
- Tests use TokioSpawner(tokio::runtime::Handle::current()) under #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)].

AppServices.spawner is passed to Session::start (SessionDeps), SchemaCatalog, run_monitor, WorkspaceStore, HistoryService, ResumeDetector and PendingSession discards.

crates/app dev-dependencies: tokio with features ["test-util", "macros", "rt"].

**Why**: Review: relm4's RUNTIME is private and real-time, so paused-clock tests could not control the tasks under test. Injection makes backoff, coalescing and deadline tests deterministic and makes the clippy allow-list truthful.

**Rejected**: - A generic spawner type parameter on Session: leaks into every consumer.
- Capturing relm4's Handle by blocking on a spawned probe at startup.
- A second runtime owned by the app.

##### D16 · SessionKey and claim before establish on every path

SessionKey = { Saved(Uuid), File(String canonical URI) }.

FileIdentity::from_gio(&gio::File) on the GTK side takes path() through std::fs::canonicalize when a path exists, and falls back to the URI. SessionKey::for_file(identity, saved) returns Saved(id) when a saved file-based connection canonicalizes to the same path, otherwise File(uri).

Picker, open() and ConnectDialog all claim first:
- ConnectDialog no longer establishes.
- On Connect it validates the form, resolves the id with find_existing_id (or Uuid::new_v4), and emits ConnectDialogOutput::Connect(ConnectIntent { key, request, pending_save }).
- SessionWindow claims. On AlreadyOpen it persists pending_save (the edits apply on the next connect, never to the live session) and presents the owner. On success it enters Connecting and persists pending_save only for the adopted attempt. Keyring store errors surface as a toast.
- TestConnection keeps establishing and discarding inside the dialog, with no claim.

**Why**: Review: ad-hoc file sessions had no key, and the dialog built a whole connection plus tunnel before discovering the connection was already open.

**Rejected**: - Keying by saved Uuid only.
- Claiming after establish.
- Saving before connecting: persists configurations that never worked, which changes current behaviour.

##### D17 · Ordered teardown for disconnect and approved close

SessionTeardown in SessionWindow:
1. CloseGuard::run returns Approved; Cancelled stops here.
2. await workspace_handle.flush(). Blocked is a no-op; a write error is logged and does not block the close.
3. The window takes SessionPage::Workspace { claim, session, workspace } out of its page. It already holds its own Arc<Session> from adoption.
4. Remove the workspace root from the adw::ToolbarView (set_content(None)) and reset the title.
5. Drop the Controller<Workspace>. Workspace::shutdown removes its window actions and disconnects its handlers.
6. Drop the claim, which releases the registry entry and may stop the ResumeDetector.
7. let closing = session.begin_shutdown(); drop(session); glib::spawn_future_local(async move { let _hold = app.hold(); log(closing.await) }).
8. Disconnect shows the Picker. Window and Quit set close_approved and call window.close().

**Why**: Review: nobody owned the shutdown call, and relm4 Controller drop never removes the child root. The claim is released before the close finishes so the same connection can be picked again at once. The old transport closes independently under its deadline.

**Rejected**: - Shutdown from Workspace Drop: the model drops later on the main context.
- Releasing the claim after the close completes: the picker in the same window would see its own claim.

##### D18 · Testable crate layout: library target, fake driver crate, process-level application tests

- crates/app gains src/lib.rs (crate tablepro_app) that owns every module. main.rs calls tablepro_app::run().
- New workspace crate crates/test-support (publish=false, dev-dependency only) provides FakeDriver and FakeConnection. They are scriptable: probe outcomes, a close delay or hang, call counters for close, list_tables and execute_in_transaction.
- Integration tests in crates/app/tests use [[test]] harness = false and run under xvfb-run -a dbus-run-session in build-linux.yml:
  - application_uniqueness.rs spawns env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tablepro-app") processes on a gio::TestDBus bus (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS from bus_address(), XDG_* pointed at tempdirs). It counts the primary's windows by introspecting <app object path>/window child nodes through gio::DBusConnection::for_address_future.
  - application_lifecycle.rs runs an in-process TableProApplication with AppServices wired to FakeDriver, checking quit and close ordering.
- Unit and #[gtk::test] tests stay in-module.

**Why**: Review: a second in-process GApplication cannot register on the singleton session bus connection (verified: attempt_primary fails when org.gtk.Application registration fails). Subprocesses on a TestDBus bus exercise real uniqueness, and the stock D-Bus window export observes the result without a test hook.

**Rejected**: - In-process second instance.
- A test-only D-Bus method.
- A self dev-dependency with a test-support feature.

##### D19 · config and GResource work for both cargo run and Meson

FA consumes this contract from the build foundation, which lands before migration step 11.

crates/app/build.rs:
- Calls glib_build_tools::compile_resources(&["data/resources"], "data/resources/resources.gresource.xml", "tablepro.gresource") (glib-build-tools 0.22.8 build-dependency; needs glib-compile-resources).
- Writes OUT_DIR/config.rs with APP_ID, PROFILE, VERSION, LOCALEDIR, RESOURCE_BASE_PATH from env TABLEPRO_APP_ID, TABLEPRO_PROFILE and TABLEPRO_LOCALEDIR. The defaults are app.tablepro.TablePro.Devel, development, CARGO_PKG_VERSION and the source po build dir.
- Declares cargo:rerun-if-env-changed for each.

Meson invokes cargo with those env vars set for release profiles.

src/config.rs does include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/config.rs")). run() calls gio::resources_register_include!("tablepro.gresource") before TableProApplication::new; an Err logs and returns ExitCode::FAILURE.

**Why**: Review: a Meson-only config.rs broke cargo run. One build.rs is the single source of config for both entry points, and a plain cargo run is the Devel profile.

**Rejected**: - Meson configure_file only: breaks cargo run.
- Hard-coded constants beside a Meson file: two sources of truth.

##### C6 · `Core Connection, DriverError and PoolPressure changes`

**Location**: `crates/core/src/{connection,error,pool_pressure,read_only}.rs; crates/drivers/*/src/lib.rs` · **Kind**: trait signature change (atomic) · **Consumers**: Session, run_monitor, PendingSession, ReadOnlyConnection, test-support FakeConnection, error_text ('The database is busy. Try again in a moment.')

```
#[async_trait] pub trait Connection: Send + Sync {
    ...
    async fn probe(&self) -> Result<(), DriverError>;   // renamed from ping
    async fn close(&self) -> Result<(), DriverError>;   // was self: Box<Self>
}
pub enum DriverError { ..., #[error("all connections are busy")] Busy }
impl DriverError { pub fn is_connection_lost(&self) -> bool; pub fn is_permanent_connect_failure(&self) -> bool; }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct PoolPressure { pub size: u32, pub idle: usize, pub max: u32 }
impl PoolPressure { pub fn is_saturated(&self) -> bool; pub fn acquire_timeout_error(&self) -> DriverError; }
```

- is_connection_lost: Disconnected, ConnectionRefused, or a Transaction whose source is lost.
- is_permanent_connect_failure: AuthFailed, Tls, IntegratedAuth.

sqlx drivers (pg, mysql, sqlite):
- map_sqlx_error(&pool, err): PoolTimedOut maps to PoolPressure { size: pool.size(), idle: pool.num_idle(), max: pool.options().get_max_connections() }.acquire_timeout_error(), which is Busy only when saturated and Disconnected otherwise.
- PoolClosed and Io other than ConnectionRefused map to Disconnected.
- PgDatabaseError code 53300 and MySqlDatabaseError::number 1040 map to Busy.
- probe: pool.try_acquire() then ping. If none is idle, a standalone <DB::Connection as sqlx::Connection>::connect_with(&pool.connect_options()), then ping, then close.
- close: pool.close().await; idempotent.

mssql:
- client: tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<MssqlClient>>; target: MssqlTarget (Clone, since tiberius Config is Clone).
- probe: client.try_lock() and SELECT 1 on the held client (None returns Disconnected). If the lock is held, open a probe client through the same spawn_blocking plus CONNECT_TIMEOUT path, run SELECT 1 and close it.
- close: takes the Option and awaits Client::close.

clickhouse: probe is the current HTTP body; close is Ok.

ReadOnlyConnection delegates both.

Server-side cancel-on-drop for fetch_rows and query is a documented trait contract implemented by the network-loss workstream (D8).
