#### W5-06 · Edit grid cells from lossless edit text with exact editors

**Step**: 42 · **Findings**: F-005, F-024, F-025  
**Depends on**: W3-06, W3-11, W4-07, W5-03, W8-16  
**Contracts**: FB-C15, FA-C15, FD-D9  
**Commit**: `fix(app): edit grid cells from lossless edit text with exact editors`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/grid/cell_editor_kind.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/inline_editor.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/multiline_editor.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/calendar_editor.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/toggle_cell.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/edit_commit.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/grid_cell.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/cell_editor.rs (deleted)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/cell_popovers.rs (deleted)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/column_factory.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/grid_menus.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/cell_preset.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/tab_grid_context.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/error_text.rs`

This is the app half of editing, on top of FB16's core C15 edit module (XW9): edit_text/EditText, parse_edit_text, empty_input_meaning, is_unchanged, EditContext and EditParseError. W5 defines no core edit API.

**Deleted.**
- grid: cell_editor.rs, cell_popovers.rs (including show_spin_button_popover), value_to_edit_text, the CellEditorKind {Int, Float, ..}, classify_editor_kind, is_bool_type, is_int_type, is_float_type, is_json_type, is_date_type, is_bytes_type and column_accepts_empty.
- browse_tab: normalize_single_line_input and whatever FB16 did not already remove of parse_input_for_column/classify_type/TypeKind/parse_*_value.

**GridCell content.** Every non-toggle cell (read-only included) now shows a `gtk::Inscription` display child, replacing the CellEditor stack and the selectable read-only Label, so GTK's label menu no longer takes Shift+F10. Text comes from the existing value_to_display_text until W5-08. Editors are created on demand.

**cell_editor_kind.rs**: `pub enum CellEditorKind { Toggle(BoolStorage), Inline { accepts_line_breaks: bool, purpose: gtk::InputPurpose }, Multiline { language: Option<&'static str> }, Calendar, ReadOnly(CellLock) }`.
- `pub fn for_cell(column: &ColumnInfo, editability: Result<(), CellLock>) -> Self`: Err(lock) gives ReadOnly(lock). By ColumnKind:
  - Bool: Toggle
  - Json: Multiline{Some("json")}; Xml: Multiline{Some("xml")}
  - Date: Calendar
  - unsigned Integer: Inline{Digits}; signed Integer, Float, Decimal, Money: Inline{Number}
  - Text, Enum, Network, Interval, Time, Timestamp, BitString, Other: Inline{accepts_line_breaks: kind accepts line breaks}
- `pub fn for_text(self, text: &EditText) -> Self`: EditText::ReadOnly(reason) gives ReadOnly(CellLock::Value(reason)). Inline escalates to Multiline{None} when the text contains '\n' or '\r', or exceeds INLINE_EDIT_MAX_BYTES = 4096.

**edit_commit.rs** (shared by every editor): `pub fn commit_edit(ctx: &TabGridContext, snapshot: &EditSnapshot, input: &str) -> CommitResult`.
- `EditContext` is InsertDraft for Draft rows and UpdateRow otherwise.
- Err(e) gives `ShowToast(error_text::edit_parse_message(&e))` and `render()`.
- A persisted row whose `is_unchanged(&original_effective, &value, ty)` gives no edit; otherwise `TrackerEdit::Cell`.
- A draft gives `TrackerEdit::DraftCell { input }`.
- Nothing is read back from the display widget.

**Effective edit value.** `TabGridContext::edit_input(row, column) -> CellInput`: the tracker input for drafts; the overlay value or `row.cells()[column]` for persisted rows. `CellInput::Value(v)` gives `edit_text(&v, &column.column_type)`; Default gives empty text with placeholder "DEFAULT".

**inline_editor.rs** (`InlineEditor`):
- begin_edit adds a `gtk::Text` as a second GridCell child and hides the Inscription.
- It sets `set_truncate_multiline(!accepts_line_breaks)`, `set_input_purpose(purpose)` and a placeholder from `empty_input_meaning` ("NULL", "DEFAULT", "Required" or none), fills the text, calls `select_region(0, -1)` and grabs focus.
- A preedit gate uses `connect_preedit_changed`, and `connect_activate` runs commit_edit.
- The Text is removed on commit or cancel.

**multiline_editor.rs** (`MultilineEditor`) is a gtk::Popover parented to the GridCell.
- A ScrolledWindow holds a `sourceview5::View` (monospace, WrapMode::WordChar, auto_indent), with the language from `sourceview5::LanguageManager::default().language(..)` and a style scheme that follows `adw::StyleManager::is_dark`.
- Cancel and Save buttons (suggested-action); a ShortcutController on the view maps `<Primary>Return` (KeyvalTrigger) to Save.
- The buffer is filled from edit_text, and Save runs commit_edit.
- `connect_closed` unparents the popover and clears `GridCell.popover`.

**calendar_editor.rs** (`CalendarEditor`):
- Only for `Value::Date(Temporal::Finite(d))` with year 1..=9999.
- `let date = glib::DateTime::from_utc(y, m, d, 0, 0, 0.0)`, then `calendar.set_date(&date)`, then `connect_day_selected`. The order matters because set_date emits day-selected when the day changes (verified in gtkcalendar.c).
- NULL on a nullable column opens on today with nothing committed until a day is picked.
- Infinities, out-of-range years or a from_utc Err open InlineEditor directly.
- day-selected formats `calendar.date().ymd()` as `%Y-%m-%d` and runs commit_edit.
- A "Type a Value" button in the popover switches to InlineEditor.

**toggle_cell.rs** (`ToggleCell`) wraps a CheckButton:
- Bool(Native) toggles Value::Bool.
- Bool(Integer): 0 is unchecked, 1 is checked, any other integer is inconsistent with the exact value in the tooltip; toggling writes Int(0) or Int(1).
- A draft Default is inconsistent with the tooltip "DEFAULT".
- `suppress_toggle` guards programmatic updates.

**Presets.** `CellPreset { Empty, Null, Default }`:
- Empty is enabled only when the kind accepts an empty string.
- Null is enabled only when the column is nullable.
- Default appears only on drafts whose column has a default or is auto-increment or generated.
- `hidden-when=action-disabled`.
- `resolve_cell_preset` uses parse_edit_text.

InsertRow seeds drafts with CellInput::Default for default, auto-increment and generated columns and Value(Null) otherwise, through `TrackerEdit::InsertDraft { cells }`.

**error_text.rs**: `pub fn edit_parse_message(error: &EditParseError) -> String` matches every variant exhaustively, with no wildcard (XW9 requires EditParseError to stay exhaustive), each to a gettext string. EditParseError's Display is logs-only and never reaches a widget.

**APIs**: gtk::Inscription (GTK 4.8) set_text; gtk::Text::set_truncate_multiline / set_input_purpose / set_placeholder_text / select_region / connect_preedit_changed / connect_activate; gtk::InputPurpose::Number / Digits; sourceview5::View / Buffer / LanguageManager::language / StyleSchemeManager (GtkSourceView 5.18, sourceview5 0.11 v5_18); gtk::WrapMode::WordChar; gtk::Calendar::set_date (GTK 4.20, gtk4 0.11 v4_20) / connect_day_selected / date; glib::DateTime::from_utc / ymd (glib 0.22); gtk::Popover::set_parent / popup / connect_closed; gtk::CheckButton::set_inconsistent / connect_toggled; gtk::ShortcutController, gtk::KeyvalTrigger::new, gtk::CallbackAction; adw::StyleManager::is_dark

**Tests**: Unit tests:
- `editor_kind_for_cell_matrix` (every ColumnKind and every CellLock)
- `inline_escalates_to_multiline_for_line_breaks_and_4096_bytes`
- `presets_enabled_per_kind_nullability_and_draft`
- `every_edit_parse_error_variant_has_a_distinct_message`: a fixture of one value per variant; messages are non-empty and pairwise distinct. The match itself is compiler-checked exhaustive.

GTK tests with TEST-SUPPORT FakeConnection:
- `unchanged_40kb_multiline_text_records_no_edit`
- `bigint_edit_is_exact` (1234567890123456789 to ...790 gives Value::Int exactly)
- `pressing_enter_on_float_keeps_full_precision` (3.14159265358979 gives no edit)
- `null_int_opens_empty_with_null_placeholder`
- `clearing_not_null_int_without_default_shows_required_toast`
- `draft_not_null_with_default_placeholder_is_default`
- `pasted_newlines_in_text_cell_are_kept`
- `tinyint1_value_2_renders_inconsistent_with_exact_tooltip`
- `calendar_preselects_date_value`
- `opening_calendar_on_existing_date_records_no_edit` (tracker summary empty after the popover opens and closes)
- `out_of_range_date_opens_inline_editor`

#### W5-07 · Make grid cells keyboard focusable with native cell navigation and keyboard menus

**Step**: 43 · **Findings**: F-004, F-025  
**Depends on**: W4-13, W4-14, W5-06, W8-14, W8-15  
**Contracts**: FD-C16, FA-C13, FA-C14  
**Commit**: `fix(app): make grid cells keyboard focusable with native navigation and keyboard menus`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/grid/grid_keyboard.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/edit_navigation.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/cell_accessibility.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/row_factory.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/column_factory.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/grid_cell.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/inline_editor.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/grid_menus.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/context_menu.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab.rs`, `data/resources/style.css`, `data/resources/shortcuts-dialog.ui`

**Focus model.**
- Every column factory setup calls `cell.set_focusable(true)`.
- `column_view.set_tab_behavior(gtk::ListTabBehavior::Cell)`: Tab leaves the grid, and the arrow keys move between cells through GtkColumnViewRowWidget's move-focus bindings.
- row_factory.rs sets `column_view.set_row_factory(Some(&factory))`; its setup calls `ColumnViewRow::set_focusable(false)`, so focus always lands on a cell.
- Deleted: the per-cell EventControllerKey (F2, Return, Tab, Left, Right), `move_focus`, the `window.child_focus` calls and the per-cell Menu ShortcutController in attach_cell_gesture. The right-click GestureClick stays.

**grid_keyboard.rs**: `GridKeyboard::install(column_view: &gtk::ColumnView, menus: GridMenus, sender: relm4::Sender<GridMsg>)` adds one `gtk::ShortcutController` with `ShortcutScope::Local` and `set_propagation_phase(PropagationPhase::Capture)`.

Hidden invariant, stated in a comment: GtkListFactoryWidget class-binds Return, ISO_Enter and KP_Enter to activate-keybinding, and space to listitem.select. A G_TYPE_NONE signal action counts as handled, so on a focused cell these keys never reach a bubble-phase ancestor controller (verified in gtklistfactorywidget.c).

Triggers use `gtk::KeyvalTrigger::new` (no parse_string/expect) and `AlternativeTrigger::new` for pairs. Each CallbackAction resolves `GridCell::from_focus(&root.focus()?)` and returns `glib::Propagation::Proceed` when there is no GridCell or `is_editing()` is true. A Proceed result lets GtkShortcutController try the next shortcut and then continue propagation (verified in gtkshortcutcontroller.c), so an open editor keeps Return (commit), Tab, Menu and `<Primary>BackSpace` (delete word). While not editing:
- `F2`, `Return`, `ISO_Enter`, `KP_Enter`: begin_edit (Toggle toggles). ReadOnly cells return Proceed, so native activation applies.
- `Menu` or `<Shift>F10`: run the same `prepare` as right-click, then `popover.set_pointing_to(Some(&bounds))` from `grid_cell.compute_bounds(&column_view)`, then popup.
- `<Primary>BackSpace`: SetCellValue Null when the cell is unlocked and nullable.

browse_tab.rs's `<Primary><Shift>n` null_shortcut is removed, because APPLICATION reserves that accel for app.new-window. Editor result grids install the same controller; there Menu opens the read-only menu.

**edit_navigation.rs** (pure): `pub fn next_edit_target(editable: &[bool], column: usize, position: u32, n_rows: u32, direction: EditDirection) -> Option<(u32, usize)>`, which wraps rows and skips locked columns.

**InlineEditor keys** (EventControllerKey on the gtk::Text, Capture):
- Tab/Shift+Tab commit, then `column_view.scroll_to(pos, Some(&columns[col]), ListScrollFlags::FOCUS, None)` and begin_edit on the new focus.
- Return commits; Escape cancels. Both return focus with `scroll_to(current, Some(&column), FOCUS, None)`.

**New draft focus.** `focus_inserted_draft` runs in `glib::idle_add_local_once`: `scroll_to(draft_position, Some(first_editable), FOCUS | SELECT, None)`, then from_focus and begin_edit.

**Accessibility** (cell_accessibility.rs, pure).
- `pub fn cell_description(state: CellPendingState) -> Option<String>` ("Modified"). `GridCell::render` calls `self.update_property(&[gtk::accessible::Property::Description(&text)])`, or `reset_property(AccessibleProperty::Description)` when None, and unbind resets it. The description is set on the GridCell, not the ColumnViewCell, because GtkColumnViewCell never forwards accessible properties (verified in gtkcolumnviewcellwidget.c).
- `pub fn row_description(state: RowPendingState) -> Option<String>` ("New row", "Marked for deletion"). row_factory bind connects the RowObject revision notify and calls `ColumnViewRow::set_accessible_description`, which GTK applies to the row widget immediately (verified in gtkcolumnviewrow.c); unbind disconnects and clears it.

**Style and shortcuts.**
- style.css replaces the `cell:focus-within > .tp-cell-editor` rule with `columnview > listview > row > cell:focus-visible > tp-grid-cell` (accent inset box-shadow).
- shortcuts-dialog.ui (AdwShortcutsDialog) gains a "Data Grid" section: F2 Edit Cell, Menu or Shift+F10 Show Cell Menu, Ctrl+Backspace Set Cell to NULL, Delete Mark Rows for Deletion, Ctrl+N Insert Row.

**APIs**: gtk::ColumnViewCell::set_focusable (GTK 4.12); gtk::ColumnView::set_tab_behavior + gtk::ListTabBehavior::Cell (GTK 4.12); gtk::ColumnView::set_row_factory, gtk::ColumnViewRow::set_focusable / set_accessible_description (GTK 4.12); gtk::ColumnView::scroll_to(pos, Some(&ColumnViewColumn), ListScrollFlags::FOCUS|SELECT, None) (GTK 4.12); gtk::ShortcutController::set_propagation_phase(PropagationPhase::Capture), ShortcutScope::Local; gtk::KeyvalTrigger::new, gtk::AlternativeTrigger::new, gtk::CallbackAction::new (-> glib::Propagation); gtk::prelude::AccessibleExtManual::update_property(&[accessible::Property::Description]), AccessibleExt::reset_property; gtk::test_accessible_has_property / test_accessible_has_role; gtk::EventControllerKey (Capture), GtkWindowExt::focus, Widget::compute_bounds, PopoverMenu::set_pointing_to; glib::idle_add_local_once; adw::ShortcutsDialog resource shortcuts-dialog.ui (libadwaita 1.8)

**Tests**: Unit tests:
- `next_edit_target_skips_locked_and_wraps_rows`
- `grid_accels_do_not_collide_with_app_accels` (<Primary>q, <Primary><Shift>n, <Primary>comma, <Primary>question)
- `cell_and_row_descriptions`

Structural GTK tests (GTK4 has no public key-event synthesis, so propagation is asserted structurally):
- `grid_shortcut_controller_runs_in_capture_phase_above_focus`: the controller's `propagation_phase()` is Capture, and `controller.widget()` is an ancestor of `window.focus()` after `scroll_to(.., FOCUS)`.
- `grid_shortcuts_proceed_while_editing`: with InlineEditor active, activating the Return, <Primary>BackSpace and Menu shortcut actions returns false (Proceed).

GTK behaviour tests (shortcut actions activated through `shortcut.action().activate(ShortcutActionFlags::empty(), &column_view, None)` after `scroll_to(.., FOCUS)`):
- `f2_starts_editing_focused_text_cell`
- `kp_enter_starts_editing_focused_int_cell`
- `return_commits_and_returns_focus_to_cell`
- `shift_f10_opens_menu_anchored_to_focused_cell`
- `ctrl_backspace_sets_focused_nullable_cell_null`
- `tab_in_edit_mode_moves_to_next_editable_column`
- `new_draft_enters_edit_mode_on_first_editable_cell`
- `focused_read_only_cell_resolves_grid_cell`

Accessibility tests:
- `pending_edit_sets_description_on_grid_cell`: `test_accessible_has_property(&grid_cell, AccessibleProperty::Description)` is true after an edit and false after Undo.
- `pending_delete_sets_row_widget_description`: `grid_cell.parent().and_then(|c| c.parent())` has role Row and the Description property.

**Step**: 44 · **Findings**: F-103, F-126  
**Depends on**: W5-07, W8-14, W8-15, W8-16, W8-20  
**Contracts**: FD-C16, FD-D9, FD-C11

#### W5-09 · Keep one owner per browse page, key rows on every identity column, and replace pages with a single splice

**Step**: 45 · **Findings**: F-004, F-103  
**Depends on**: W2-11, W3-05, W3-06, W4-10, W5-08  
**Contracts**: META, RESULT, FA-C11, FB-C14  
**Commit**: `perf(app): keep one owner per browse page and key rows on every identity column`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/grid/row_snapshot.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/row_key_builder.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/tab_grid_context.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/selection.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/column_factory.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/page_state.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/editor.rs`

**Page layout** comes from the page builder (XW13). `PageSpec.layout: PageLayout { visible: Range<usize>, identity: Range<usize> }`, where `identity == visible.end..visible.end + k`; k is 0 for UniqueKey, 1 for ctid or rowid, and 2 for tableoid,ctid.

**row_key_builder.rs**: `pub struct RowKeyBuilder { source: KeySource }` with `enum KeySource { Visible(Box<[usize]>), Identity(Range<usize>) }`.
- `pub fn for_page(identity: &RowIdentity, columns: &[ColumnInfo], layout: &PageLayout) -> Option<Self>`:
  - UniqueKey gives the key column indices within the visible range.
  - EngineRowId gives the whole identity range, so tableoid and ctid both enter the key and a ctid from another partition can never match.
  - SortingKey and Unordered give None; those rows are Unkeyed and locked.
- `pub fn key_for(&self, visible: &[Value], identity: &[Value]) -> Option<RowKey>` builds `RowKey::Persisted(Vec<ValueIdentity>)` and returns None when a key cell is Undecodable.

**Page load.** The Page reply handler destructures `QueryResult { columns, rows, truncated }`. For each row:
1. `let identity = row.split_off(layout.visible.end)`.
2. `let key = builder.key_for(&row, &identity)`.
3. `RowObject::persisted(key, Arc::from(row))`.

Values are moved, never cloned, and identity cells are dropped once the key is built. RowObjects therefore hold only visible cells, so effective_cells, RowSnapshot, Copy as INSERT, Duplicate, clipboard and page export can never see ctid, tableoid or rowid. Drafts from `handle.drafts()` are prepended, then one `store.splice(0, store.n_items(), &objects)` and `index.rebuild(&store)`.

**page_state.rs**: `pub struct PageState { pub result_columns: Arc<[ResultColumn]>, pub layout: PageLayout, pub truncated: bool, pub row_count: usize, pub start_ordinal: u64 }` replaces `current_result: Option<QueryResult>`. `result_columns` is sliced to `layout.visible`.
- Deleted: `BrowseTab::snapshot()`, `export_payload`, the `current_result.clone()` in render_grid_if_ready, the refresh_grid_data append loop and `reprepend_drafts`.
- `build_column_view` takes `columns: &[ColumnInfo]` and `Vec<RowObject>`, not `&QueryResult`.

**row_snapshot.rs**: `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct RowSnapshot { cells: Arc<[Value]>, overrides: Box<[(usize, Value)]> }` (Send), with `value(&self, column) -> &Value` and `len()`.
- `TabGridContext::snapshot(&self, row) -> RowSnapshot` clones the Arc plus only the modified values.
- Draft snapshots come from tracker CellInputs, with Default rendered as NULL.
- `rows_for_menu` and `export_snapshot` return `Vec<RowSnapshot>`.

Editor results build `RowObject::result(Arc::from(row))` by moving rows.

**APIs**: gio::ListStore::splice (GLib 2.44); std::sync::Arc<[Value]> via Arc::from(Vec<T>), Vec::split_off

- `row_key_builder_unique_key_uses_visible_key_columns`
- `row_key_builder_tableoid_ctid_keys_on_both_identity_columns` (rows with equal ctid and different tableoid get distinct keys)
- `row_key_builder_rowid_uses_single_identity_column`

#### W5-10 · Refresh browse tabs in place and keep the last good page when a reload fails

**Step**: 46 · **Findings**: F-102  
**Depends on**: W2-11, W4-01, W4-06, W4-10, W4-13, W4-14, W5-09  
**Contracts**: FA-C11, FA-C13, FA-C14, CATALOG, SESSION, ERR, TEST-SUPPORT

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/tab_load/mod.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/tab_load/content_load.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/tab_load/load_presentation.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/tab_load/load_failure.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/tab_load/stale_banner.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/selection_snapshot.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/workspace/tabs.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/workspace/sidebar.rs`

**content_load.rs** (pure, GTK-free): `pub enum ContentLoad { Initial, Loading, Loaded, Refreshing, Stale(LoadFailure), Failed(LoadFailure) }` with `begin`, `succeed` and `fail(LoadFailure)`, each returning LoadPresentation.

**load_presentation.rs**: `pub struct LoadPresentation { pub page: ContentPage, pub tab_loading: bool, pub stale: Option<LoadFailure> }` and `pub enum ContentPage { Spinner, Content, Error(LoadFailure) }`.

Transitions:
- Initial or Failed, then begin: Loading, Spinner, tab_loading.
- Loaded or Stale, then begin: Refreshing, Content, tab_loading; the banner stays until success.
- Loading, then fail: Failed, Error.
- Refreshing, then fail: Stale, Content, stale Some.
- Any state, then succeed: Loaded, Content, tab_loading false, stale None.

**load_failure.rs**: `#[derive(Debug, Clone)] pub enum LoadFailure { Columns(Arc<OperationError>), NoColumns, ColumnsChanged, Page(Arc<OperationError>) }`. `pub fn message(&self) -> String` maps through error_text by `DriverError::category()` (OperationError::Sql by builder variant) and never uses markup.

**stale_banner.rs** (`StaleBanner`) is an `adw::Banner` in a ToolbarView top bar, with a caller-supplied title and `set_button_label(Some(&gettext("Retry")))`. `connect_button_clicked` sends Refresh, and the tooltip carries the failure message. Browse title: "Couldn't refresh rows. Showing the last loaded page."

**BrowseTab** holds `load: ContentLoad` and applies each presentation:
- Spinner and Error use the inner Stack. The error `adw::StatusPage` "Couldn't Load Rows" gets a `.pill .suggested-action` "Try Again" button sending Refresh.
- `tab_loading` goes out as `BrowseTabOutput::LoadingChanged(bool)`, and Workspace tabs.rs calls `adw::TabPage::set_loading`.
- Refresh no longer calls show_loading_inner when content exists.
- ShowError no longer clears the page, total or paginator.

**selection_snapshot.rs**: `pub struct SelectionSnapshot { keys: Vec<RowKey>, focus: Option<(RowKey, usize)> }`.
- `capture(selection, column_view)` reads keys from RowObjects and the focused GridCell.
- `restore(&self, index: &GridRowIndex, store, selection, column_view, columns: &[gtk::ColumnViewColumn])` builds a gtk::Bitset of found positions, calls `selection.set_selection(&selected, &mask)` over 0..n_items and `scroll_to(pos, Some(&columns[col]), ListScrollFlags::FOCUS, None)`.
- It replaces `capture_focus_for_restore` and `restore_focused_row`.

**Sidebar.** sidebar.rs calls `sync_sidebar_selection()` after every applied catalog snapshot.

**APIs**: adw::TabPage::set_loading (libadwaita 1.0); adw::Banner::set_title / set_button_label(Option<&str>) / connect_button_clicked / set_revealed (libadwaita 1.3); adw::StatusPage, gtk::Button with .pill / .suggested-action; gtk::SelectionModelExt::set_selection(&gtk::Bitset, &gtk::Bitset), gtk::Bitset::new_empty / add / add_range; gtk::ColumnView::scroll_to with ListScrollFlags::FOCUS (GTK 4.12); adw::ToolbarView::add_top_bar

#### W5-11 · Keep loaded structure on screen when a structure refresh fails and refetch columns after schema saves

**Step**: 47 · **Findings**: F-102  
**Depends on**: W4-06, W4-10, W4-12, W5-10  
**Contracts**: FA-C11, FA-C16, CATALOG, SESSION, SAVE  
**Commit**: `fix(app): keep loaded structure on screen when a structure refresh fails`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/structure_tab/mod.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/structure_tab/structure_fetch.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/workspace/tabs.rs`

**StructureTab** owns `load: ContentLoad` (W5-10) and a StaleBanner titled (gettext) "Couldn't reload structure. Showing the last loaded version."
- The inner stack's "loading" page is used only for `ContentPage::Spinner`.
- Try Again, Retry and the post-save refetch call `load.begin()` and no longer show "loading" when a snapshot exists.
- `StructureTabOutput::LoadingChanged(bool)` drives `adw::TabPage::set_loading`.
- `StructureTabInput::LoadFailed` runs `load.fail(..)`. With a snapshot it keeps the "editor" page and the original_* snapshots, reveals the banner and sets `refetching` to false. Without one it shows the error StatusPage.
- Status and error text is plain (F-027 rule).

**structure_fetch.rs** replaces App::on_fetch_structure_data (moved into the tab by FA8): `pub async fn fetch_structure(session: Arc<Session>, table: TableRef, freshness: ColumnFreshness, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<StructureSnapshot, LoadFailure>` with `pub enum ColumnFreshness { Cached, Refetch }`.
- Cached (first open) uses `session.columns(table)`. Refetch (Retry, Try Again, and after `SaveOutcome::Committed` for `Save(WriteKind::SchemaChanges)`) uses `session.refresh_columns(table)` (XW14). The column cache is never shown stale beside fresh indexes and foreign keys, and a failed refetch keeps the cached columns (never-clear).
- `fetch_indexes` and `fetch_foreign_keys` run under `session.run_cancellable(OperationKind::Metadata, ..)`.
- Any failure fails the whole snapshot, removing the `unwrap_or_default()` that replaced good index and foreign-key lists with empty ones. Empty columns give LoadFailure::NoColumns.

#### W5-12 · Fail browse tabs visibly when columns cannot be loaded and refetch columns on refresh

**Step**: 47 · **Findings**: F-100  
**Depends on**: W4-01, W4-06, W4-10, W5-09, W5-10  
**Contracts**: FA-C11, CATALOG, SESSION, TEST-SUPPORT  
**Commit**: `fix(app): surface browse column fetch failures and refetch columns on refresh`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/columns_fetch.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/column_recheck.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/browse_request_kind.rs`

**columns_fetch.rs**: `pub async fn load_columns(session: Arc<Session>, table: TableRef, freshness: ColumnFreshness) -> Result<Arc<[ColumnInfo]>, LoadFailure>`.
- Cached uses `session.columns(table)`; Refetch uses `session.refresh_columns(table)` (XW14, never clears).
- Err gives `LoadFailure::Columns(err)`.
- An empty list gives `LoadFailure::NoColumns`, with message (gettext) "This table has no columns you can read. It may have been dropped, or your account can't read it."
- Every failure logs `tracing::warn!(schema = ?table.schema, table = %table.name, category = ?category, "browse columns failed")`, without SQL or credentials.

**Fetch ordering.** The page request is issued only after columns resolve, because page projections need ColumnInfo. A columns failure runs `load.fail` right away, so the tab can never stay on the spinner. `BrowseRequestKind::Columns` is sequenced by RequestSequencer, and superseded replies are dropped.

**Refresh and Retry.** Load columns with Refetch, then on success issue Page plus the W5-13 estimate and count requests. First open uses Cached.

**column_recheck.rs**: `pub struct ColumnRecheck { attempted: bool }` with `pub fn check(&mut self, columns: &[ColumnInfo], result_columns: &[ResultColumn], layout: &PageLayout) -> RecheckAction { Accept, Refetch, Fail }`.
- Accept when `result_columns.len() == layout.visible.len() + layout.identity.len()` and the names in `layout.visible` equal `columns` in order.
- The first mismatch gives Refetch (columns with Refetch, then the page again).
- A second mismatch gives Fail(LoadFailure::ColumnsChanged).
- Accept resets the guard.

**APIs**: tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken via RequestSequencer (FA C11); tracing::warn!

- `column_recheck_accepts_matching_visible_names_with_identity_tail`

#### W5-13 · Show row count estimates and count exact totals on demand

**Step**: 48 · **Findings**: F-042  
**Depends on**: W2-11, W2-15, W3-06, W4-01, W4-06, W4-10, W4-12, W5-10, W5-12  
**Contracts**: FA-C11, FA-C16, CONN, SESSION, SAVE, META, TEST-SUPPORT, FB-C14  
**Commit**: `feat(app): show row count estimates and count exact totals on demand`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/row_total.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/count_policy.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/count_failure_text.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/browse_pager.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab/browse_request_kind.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/browse_tab.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/format/mod.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/format/thousands.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/workspace/tabs.rs`

**row_total.rs**: `pub enum RowTotal { Unknown, Estimated(u64), Counting { estimate: Option<u64> }, Exact(u64), Unavailable { estimate: Option<u64>, reason: String } }` with:
- `paginator_label(&self, start: u64, end: u64) -> String`: "Rows 1 – 1,000 of 5,000", "Rows 1 – 1,000 of about 5,000,000", or "Rows 1 – 1,000". It uses `format_thousands`, moved from browse_tab.rs to ui/format/thousands.rs as `pub fn format_thousands(n: u64) -> String`.
- `exact(&self) -> Option<u64>`.
- `adjust_after_save(&mut self, inserted: u64, deleted: u64, filtered: bool)` (saturating): unfiltered Exact stays Exact; filtered Exact becomes Estimated, because inserted or updated rows may not match the filter; Estimated stays Estimated.

**count_policy.rs**: `pub const AUTO_COUNT_MAX_ROWS: u64 = 100_000;` and `pub fn decide(estimate: Result<&RowCountEstimate, ()>) -> CountAction { UseExact(u64), UseEstimate(u64), CountNow, OfferCount }`:
- Exact(n) unfiltered: UseExact.
- Approximate(n) with n ≤ AUTO_COUNT_MAX_ROWS: CountNow, a count bounded by the small table's size.
- Approximate(n) above the limit: UseEstimate plus OfferCount.
- Unknown: OfferCount, never an automatic count. table_estimate reports Unknown without server work for engines with no estimate (SQLite) and for PostgreSQL reltuples = -1, so SQLite counts on demand as the audit requires.
- An estimate error: OfferCount.
- When filtered, an Exact estimate is not used as the filtered total, and the unfiltered estimate drives CountNow versus OfferCount.

**Requests.** BrowseRequestKind gains Estimate and Count.
- Open, refresh and filter apply issue Estimate: `session.run_cancellable(OperationKind::Metadata, &ticket.cancel, |lease, o| async move { lease.table_estimate(&table, o).await.map_err(OperationError::from) })`.
- An estimate Err sets `RowTotal::Unknown`, offers Count Rows and logs `tracing::warn!(category = ?e.category(), "row estimate unavailable")`.
- CountNow and the button issue Count: `run_cancellable(OperationKind::Count, ..)`. `browse::build_count(&*lease.dialect(), ..)?` is built inside the op, then `lease.count_rows(&statement, o)`.
- A new filter, refresh or tab close supersedes or drops the ticket, which cancels the CallOptions token; the driver stops the server statement (CONN rule 1).
- Replies apply only when `sequencer.accept(kind, stamp)`.

**count_failure_text.rs**: `pub fn count_failure_text(error: &OperationError, count_deadline: Option<Duration>) -> String`. `DriverError::Timeout{..}` with Some(d) gives ngettext_f "Counting took longer than {seconds} second and was stopped." / "... seconds ..." from `d.as_secs()`; everything else uses error_text by category. `BrowseTabInit` gains `deadlines: Arc<dyn DeadlinePolicy>`, injected by Workspace tabs.rs from SessionDeps, and the message reads `deadlines.deadline(OperationKind::Count)`. A count Err gives `RowTotal::Unavailable { reason }`; nothing is silently dropped.

**Paginator UI** (gtk::ActionBar):
- A flat "Count Rows" button, visible unless the total is Exact. While Counting its child is an adw::Spinner with "Counting…" and it is insensitive; for Unavailable it reads "Try Again" with the reason as tooltip.
- Last is sensitive only when `total.exact()` is Some, with tooltip otherwise "Count rows to go to the last page".
- Clamp-and-refetch runs only on an accepted Exact total.

**browse_pager.rs**: `pub struct BrowsePager { page_size: u64, start_ordinal: u64 }` with first/next/prev/last returning `Option<(PagePosition, u64)>`. Last requires `RowTotal::Exact`, and positions are PagePosition::Offset. W2's F-055 keyset work extends this type (XW12 depends on this task).

**Save.** On `SaveOutcome::Committed`, `total.adjust_after_save(origins.inserts, origins.deletes, filter.is_active())` counts SavePlan ChangeOrigin entries, and the post-save FetchRowCount is removed. `App::fetch_browse_row_count` and `AppMsg::RowCountLoaded` are deleted.

**APIs**: adw::Spinner (libadwaita 1.6); gtk::ActionBar / gtk::Button / gtk::Box; tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken through RequestSequencer (FA C11); gettext ngettext_f (FD C11)

**Tests**: Unit tests:
- `count_policy_table` (Exact, Approximate ≤ and > 100,000, Unknown, estimate error, filtered variants)
- `row_total_labels_use_thousands_and_about`
- `adjust_after_save_keeps_exact_only_when_unfiltered`
- `row_total_adjust_is_saturating`
- `count_failure_text_uses_policy_deadline` (a 45 s policy gives "45 seconds")
- `browse_pager_last_requires_exact_total`
- `format_thousands_edges`

- export_sink_parts.rs: `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct ExportSinkParts { pub messages: async_channel::Sender<ExportMessage>, pub format: ExportFormat, pub csv: CsvOptions }` with `pub fn sink(&self) -> EncodingSink`.

**encoding_sink.rs**: `pub struct EncodingSink { parts: ExportSinkParts, encoder: Option<Box<dyn RowEncoder>>, buffer: Vec<u8>, rows: u64, result_sets: u32 }` implements the EDITOR `ResultSink` (async_trait, Send + 'static), consuming the FC-C9 event sequence ResultSetStarted, Rows, ResultSetFinished:
- ResultSetStarted { columns }: the encoder is created lazily from these stream columns (`format.encoder(columns, &csv)`) and `begin` runs. A second result set sends `Failed(MultipleResultSets)` and returns SinkFlow::ConsumerGone.
- Rows: encode each row; once the buffer reaches CHUNK_BYTES = 64 KiB, `messages.send(Chunk{..}).await`. The channel is `async_channel::bounded(4)`, so a slow disk pauses the stream and TCP backpressure reaches the server (FC-D20). A send error returns ConsumerGone.
- An EncodeError sends Failed(Encode) and returns ConsumerGone.
- ResultSetFinished: finish, flush, send Finished.
- Other events: Continue.

**export_producer.rs**: `pub fn start_rows_producer(spawner: &Arc<dyn TaskSpawner>, columns: Arc<[ResultColumn]>, rows: Vec<RowSnapshot>, parts: ExportSinkParts, cancel: CancellationToken) -> TaskResult<()>`. Inside `spawner.spawn_task` it drives the same EncodingSink with synthesized ResultSetStarted, Rows (256-row batches) and ResultSetFinished events, checking `cancel` between batches, off the GTK thread.

**replace_file_writer.rs** (`ReplaceFileWriter`, main context, !Send).

`pub async fn open(file: &gio::File) -> Result<Self, glib::Error>`:
1. `file.create_future(FileCreateFlags::NONE, Priority::DEFAULT)`; Ok gives strategy `Created`.
2. On IOErrorEnum::Exists: `query_info_future(FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ETAG_VALUE, FileQueryInfoFlags::NONE, ..)` records `before_etag`, then `replace_future(None, false, FileCreateFlags::NONE, Priority::DEFAULT)` gives strategy `Replaced`. There is no REPLACE_DESTINATION flag, so symlinks are written through as GtkSourceFileSaver does.

Other methods:
- `write(&self, chunk: Vec<u8>)` calls `write_all_future` and treats `Ok((_, _, Some(err)))` as failure.
- `finish(self)` calls `close_future`.
- `pub async fn abort(self) -> AbortOutcome`: close with a pre-cancelled `gio::Cancellable`. Created: `delete_future`, giving `Removed`. Replaced: re-query the etag; equal gives `Untouched`, different gives `Incomplete`.
- `impl Drop` for an unfinished writer spawns the same abort through `glib::spawn_future_local`.

Hidden invariant, in a comment: a local replace stream renames its temp file over the destination on close unless close sees a cancelled cancellable, and dispose closes without one. GLib takes the temp-file path only for an existing single-link regular file whose directory accepts the temp file; otherwise it truncates the destination at open. So abort guarantees Untouched only on that path, and the etag comparison reports the other cases (verified in glocalfileoutputstream.c: O_CREAT|O_EXCL first, the handle_overwrite_open condition, the ftruncate fallback, and the cancel check before rename).

**Pipeline.** `ExportLedger::begin(job)` runs `glib::spawn_future_local`:
1. Open the writer.
2. Start the producer (Rows here, Query in W5-16).
3. Loop `messages.recv().await`: Chunk writes and updates progress; Failed and cancel abort; Finished finishes. A closed channel with the producer TaskResult Err aborts with that error.

It holds `app.hold()` (ApplicationHoldGuard) for the job.

**export_ledger.rs** (`ExportLedger`, one per Workspace):
- `begin(&self, job) -> ExportJobHandle`, `in_flight()`, `when_idle() -> impl Future`, `cancel_all()`.
- While in_flight > 0 it holds `gtk::Application::inhibit(Some(&window), ApplicationInhibitFlags::LOGOUT | ApplicationInhibitFlags::SUSPEND, Some(&gettext("Exporting data")))`, where cookie 0 means not inhibited, and releases it with uninhibit.
- `impl CloseBlocker for ExportLedger` (the FA10 seam, XW5): `blocking()` returns `CloseBlockPrompt { heading: "Stop Exports?", body: ngettext_f("{n} export is still running. Stopping it leaves the file unfinished.", ..), keep_label: "Keep Exporting", stop_label: "Stop Exports" }` when in_flight > 0; `stop()` runs cancel_all then when_idle.
- This commit adds `Workspace::exports() -> Rc<ExportLedger>` and registers the ledger with `Workspace::register_close_blocker`.

**export_operations_button.rs** (`ExportOperationsButton`, following the GNOME Files operations button and Epiphany downloads popover):

- Its popover holds a `.boxed-list` ListBox with one row per job:

  - a `gtk::ProgressBar`: `set_fraction` when a fraction exists, `pulse()` otherwise
  - subtitle: ngettext_f "{rows} row of about {total}" / "{rows} rows of about {total}", or "{rows} rows"
  - a flat `process-stop-symbolic` "Stop Export" button

**export_failure_text.rs** maps outcomes to text:

**export_query.rs**: `#[derive(Clone)] pub enum ExportQuery { Table(TableExport), Editor { sql: UserSql } }` and `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct TableExport { pub table: TableRef, pub columns: Arc<[ColumnInfo]>, pub filter: FilterSet, pub sort: Vec<SortKey>, pub identity: RowIdentity }` with `pub fn request(&self) -> ExportRequest<'_>` (XW3).

**export_producer.rs** adds `pub fn start_query_producer(spawner: &Arc<dyn TaskSpawner>, session: Arc<Session>, query: ExportQuery, parts: ExportSinkParts, cancel: CancellationToken) -> TaskResult<Result<StreamSummary, OperationError>>`. It runs inside `spawner.spawn_task` (RUNTIME tokio-context rule):
```rust
let query = Arc::new(query);
session.run_cancellable(OperationKind::Export, &cancel, move |lease: ConnectionLease, options: CallOptions| {
    let parts = parts.clone();
    let query = Arc::clone(&query);
    async move {
        let read = match &*query {
            ExportQuery::Table(export) => ReadStatement::Generated(browse::build_export(&*lease.dialect(), &export.request())?),
            ExportQuery::Editor { sql } => ReadStatement::User(sql.clone()),
        };
        let summary = lease.stream_read(&read, Box::new(parts.sink()), CallOptions::new(options.deadline, options.cancel.clone())).await?;
        Ok(summary)
    }
}).await
```
- The op is Fn: it clones Clone parts per call and never clones EncodingSink.
- `?` converts BrowseSqlError and DriverError through OperationError's From impls (SESSION). SQL is built from the lease that streams it.
- Export's deadline is None (XW2), and the encoder header comes from the stream's own columns (W5-15).
- The ledger's main-context loop joins this TaskResult with the channel.

**Editor All Rows** re-runs only the statement that produced the result tab (its UserSql, W5-17) on a separate read-only connection (XW1). Failures read:
- `Failed(MultipleResultSets)`: "This statement returned more than one result, so it can't be exported as one file."
- category ReadOnly: "Export All only runs statements that read data. This statement changes data."
- category Server: "Export All runs the statement again on a separate connection, so temporary tables, session settings and uncommitted changes from this editor aren't available." plus a blank line and the plain server message.

**export_scope.rs**: `pub enum ExportOrigin { Browse { page: ExportSource, query: ExportQuery, total: RowTotal, has_unsaved_changes: bool }, Editor { shown: ExportSource, query: ExportQuery, shown_rows: u64, truncated: bool } }` and `pub fn scope_choices(origin: &ExportOrigin) -> Vec<ScopeChoice>` with `ScopeChoice { title: String, subtitle: String, source: ScopeSource }`.
- Browse offers "Current Page" (ngettext_f "{n} row" / "{n} rows") and "Entire Table" ("{n} rows" when Exact, "about {n} rows" when Estimated, adding "Filters apply" when a filter is set). has_unsaved_changes adds "Unsaved changes aren't included".
- Editor offers "Shown Rows" and "All Rows" ("Runs the statement again on a separate read-only connection"); All Rows is preselected when truncated.

**export_dialog.rs** gains an `adw::ComboRow` "Rows" over a gtk::StringList of scope titles, whose subtitle updates on `connect_selected_notify`, beside the Format ComboRow.

#### W5-18 · Sort editor result grids by column header

**Step**: 51 · **Findings**: F-127  
**Depends on**: W5-02, W5-08, W5-17  
**Contracts**: RESULT  
**Commit**: `feat(app): sort editor result grids by column header`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/grid/value_order.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/result_sorters.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/result_grid.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/grid/column_factory.rs`, `crates/app/src/ui/result_pane/mod.rs`

**value_order.rs** (pure, no text collation): `pub fn compare(a: &Value, b: &Value, column: &ColumnType) -> std::cmp::Ordering` for non-text kinds.
- NULL first.
- Numbers compare across Int, UInt, WideInt, Float32/64 and Decimal by value, using `SqlDecimal::cmp_numeric` and i128/WideInteger widening. NaN sorts after every number; floats use `total_cmp` within a class.
- Temporals order NegInfinity < Finite < Infinity; offset timestamps compare by UTC instant, then offset.
- Bytes are lexicographic; Bool is false < true; Uuid compares bytes; Bits compares length then bytes; Array is element-wise.
- `pub fn storage_class_order(a, b) -> Ordering` for dynamic_storage columns: null < numeric (compared numerically) < text (Equal here) < blob.
- `pub fn sort_text(value: &Value) -> Option<&str>` returns text for Text, JsonText, Other, Enum and Network values.

**result_sorters.rs**: `pub fn column_sorter(index: usize, column: &ResultColumn) -> gtk::Sorter`.
- Text kinds: a `gtk::MultiSorter` of a CustomSorter ordering NULL before non-NULL, then `gtk::StringSorter::new(Some(ClosureExpression::with_callback(&[] as &[gtk::Expression], move |v| row_text(v, index))))` with `set_collation(gtk::Collation::Unicode)`. GtkStringSorter builds a `g_utf8_collate_key` once per item and compares keys with strcmp (verified in gtkstringsorter.c), so a 10,000-row sort does not normalise strings per comparison.
- dynamic_storage: a MultiSorter of a CustomSorter over storage_class_order, then the same StringSorter, whose expression returns text only for text-class values.
- Every other kind: a `gtk::CustomSorter` over value_order::compare.

**result_grid.rs**: `pub fn build_result_grid(columns: Arc<[ResultColumn]>, rows: Vec<RowObject>, sender: relm4::Sender<GridMsg>) -> ResultGrid { column_view, selection }`. It chains gio::ListStore, `gtk::SortListModel::new(Some(store), column_view.sorter())` with `set_incremental(false)`, gtk::MultiSelection and the ColumnView, and calls `column.set_sorter(Some(&column_sorter(i, col)))`. Server-sorted browse grids keep the equal CustomSorter. Copy, menu and export resolve rows through GridCell::row (W5-02), so they act on the displayed row.

- Csv: "text/csv"

It renders through `spawn_blocking_task` with the W5-14 encoders, or FB C16 render_in_clause and render_insert with the dialect captured on the GTK thread from `session.current_dialect()`. **row_json_dialog.rs** renders off-thread. The buffer shows string values longer than 10,000 chars cut at a char boundary with "… ({count} more bytes)", and an adw::Banner reads "Long values are shortened here. Copy includes them in full." Copy writes the complete JSON as application/json plus text/plain.

#### Needs from other workstreams (resolved in the overview's conflict list)

- XW1-stream-read (W2 drivers, FC CONN owner). CONN needs `async fn stream_read(&self, read: &ReadStatement, sink: Box<dyn ResultSink>, o: CallOptions) -> Result<StreamSummary, DriverError>` with `pub enum ReadStatement { Generated(Statement), User(UserSql) }` and `pub struct StreamSummary { pub rows: u64 }`.
- It runs on a standalone physical connection opened through the driver's establish path (like CONN rule 3's probe), never a pool slot.
- No row limit; ResultSink backpressure per FC-D20; deadline from CallOptions (None for export); server stop on cancel per FC-C18.
- It emits the FC-C9 sequence ResultSetStarted { columns: Arc<[ResultColumn]> }, then Rows, then ResultSetFinished for each result set.
- Engine-enforced read-only scope:
  - PostgreSQL: START TRANSACTION READ ONLY with SET LOCAL statement_timeout 0 (extended protocol).
  - MySQL/MariaDB: START TRANSACTION READ ONLY.
  - SQLite: read-only open.
  - ClickHouse: readonly=2.
  - SQL Server: BEGIN TRANSACTION then ROLLBACK.
- A write attempt surfaces as category ReadOnly.
- TEST-SUPPORT FakeConnection scripts stream_read batches and records CallOptions.
- XW2-operation-kind-export (FA SESSION owner): add `OperationKind::Export`. DefaultDeadlines returns None for it, is_replayable is false, and the runner adds no timer.
- XW3-build-export (W3 core browse, FB owner): add `browse::build_export(&dyn SqlDialect, &ExportRequest<'_> { table: &TableRef, columns: &[ColumnInfo], filter: &FilterSet, sort: &[SortKey], identity: &RowIdentity }) -> Result<Statement, BrowseSqlError>`. It uses the same column projections and filter as build_page but never projects engine_row_id columns (no ctid, tableoid or rowid in the SELECT list). It orders by the user sort plus an identity tiebreak (UniqueKey columns, or the engine row id used only in ORDER BY), with no LIMIT or OFFSET, and a test asserts the projection list equals the visible columns.
- XW4-tracker-delta-shape (FA C15 owner). TabTrackerHandle returns `TrackerDelta { changed: Vec<RowKey>, inserted_drafts: Vec<DraftId>, removed_drafts: Vec<DraftId>, pending_count: usize }` from apply, undo, redo, discard and settle_save.
- discard_draft, undo of an insert and Discard emit removed_drafts; redo of an insert emits inserted_drafts.
- Draft cells are stored as core CellInput.
- TrackerEdit variants:
  - `Cell { key, column, original: Value, new: Value }`
  - `DraftCell { draft, column, input: CellInput }`
  - `InsertDraft { cells: Vec<CellInput> }`
  - `DeleteRows { persisted: Vec<(RowKey, Arc<[Value]>)>, drafts: Vec<DraftId> }`
- `cell_overlay` returns an owned value only for modified cells.

W5-02 is the first consumer.
- XW5-close-blocker-seam (FA10 save ledger and CloseGuard; this removes the former cycle). FA10 lands a W5-independent seam: `pub trait CloseBlocker { fn blocking(&self) -> Option<CloseBlockPrompt>; fn stop(&self) -> LocalBoxFuture<'static, ()>; }`, `pub struct CloseBlockPrompt { pub heading: String, pub body: String, pub keep_label: String, pub stop_label: String }` and `Workspace::register_close_blocker(&self, Rc<dyn CloseBlocker>)`.
- CloseGuard and QuitSequence consult every blocker before approving and show an adw::AlertDialog built from the prompt, with keep as the close response and stop as destructive.
- The stop response awaits `stop()` before continuing.

W5-15 implements the trait for ExportLedger, registers it, and adds Workspace::exports() itself.
- XW6-session-header (W7 window shell; this removes the former dependency). W5-15 packs ExportOperationsButton at the end of the FA11 SessionWindow header bar, and W5-07 adds the Data Grid section to shortcuts-dialog.ui. W7 tasks that restructure the SessionWindow header or shortcuts-dialog.ui depend on W5-15 and W5-07 and keep those items.
- XW7-editor-result-pane (W6 SQL editor; this removes the former cycle). W5-17 owns the editor.rs hand-off to ResultPane (ResultSetView with the originating UserSql and ResultSummary) and history_row_count. W6 tasks touching editor result rendering or history row counts depend on W5-17. W6 tasks touching history_dialog.rs file writes depend on W5-15, which moves save_export onto ReplaceFileWriter.
- XW8-decode-as-rows-arrive (W2 drivers, part of F-103): every query_bound and stream_read implementation decodes each protocol row into Vec<Value> as it arrives (tokio-postgres RowStream, sqlx fetch, tiberius QueryStream, the ClickHouse cursor), never collecting raw driver rows first. A per-driver conformance test runs a 50,000-row wide query and asserts raw-row buffering stays bounded.
- XW9-fb-edit-ordering (FB16-edit, blocking prerequisite of W5-06). W5 defines no core edit API. FB16 must land the C15 edit module with:
- `edit_text(&Value, &ColumnType) -> EditText { Editable(String), ReadOnly(ReadOnlyReason) }`: never truncates or normalises.
- `parse_edit_text(&str, &ColumnInfo, EditContext) -> Result<CellInput, EditParseError>`: exact integer and decimal bounds, shortest round-trip floats, infinity words, and the FB D15 empty-input rules per EditContext.
- `empty_input_meaning(&ColumnInfo, EditContext) -> EmptyInputMeaning`, sharing the parse rule.
- `is_unchanged(&Value, &Value, &ColumnType) -> bool`.

EditParseError is a thiserror enum that is NOT #[non_exhaustive], so the app's gettext mapping is compiler-checked exhaustive. Its Display is for logs only.

FB16's app half is limited to switching browse_tab.rs's commit path from parse_input_for_column to parse_edit_text (deleting parse_input_for_column, classify_type, TypeKind, parse_*_value and their tests). W5-06 owns every other editor change (spin popovers, normalize_single_line_input, the grid string classifiers, and the new editors).
- XW10-export-encoders (FB17 owner, plus DEPS FD/W8 and RUNTIME FA). FB17's export split lands before W5-14. W5-14 removes serde_json preserve_order from the workspace Cargo.toml and adds `disallowed-types` serde_json::Map and `disallowed-methods` serde_json::Value::as_object/as_object_mut to linux/clippy.toml and crates/app/clippy.toml, as CI shared keys, in the same commit. DEPS and RUNTIME contracts must record both, and later commits must not re-add the feature.
- XW11-style-css (W8, FD C16 owner). style.css selectors change with W5:
- `.tp-cell-editor` becomes the `tp-grid-cell` CSS node.
- The focus rule targets `columnview > listview > row > cell:focus-visible > tp-grid-cell`.
- `label.tp-null-sentinel` is removed, because placeholders use Pango italic attributes.

The pending-state classes stay. W8's CSS work depends on W5-07 and W5-08.
- XW12-paging-mode (W2, F-055 owner; this reverses the former dependency). W2's F-055 keyset and ctid-window task depends on W5-13. It extends BrowsePager and derives AfterKey/BeforeKey anchors from W5's GridRowIndex boundary rows instead of adding parallel paging state, and it exports a shared core rule `browse::paging_mode(&RowIdentity, &[SortKey]) -> PagingMode { Keyset, CtidWindow, Offset }` so builder and pager cannot disagree.
- XW13-page-layout (W3 core browse, FB build_page owner): `PageSpec` must expose `layout: PageLayout { visible: Range<usize>, identity: Range<usize> }`, with identity columns appended right after the visible ones (identity == visible.end..visible.end + k). k is 0 for UniqueKey, 1 for PostgresCtid or SqliteRowid, and 2 for PostgresTableoidCtid (both tableoid and ctid). A builder test covers each case. W5-09 keys rows on the whole identity range, and W5-12 validates the width.
- XW14-refresh-columns (FA SESSION and CATALOG owner): add `Session::refresh_columns(&self, table: TableRef) -> Result<Arc<[ColumnInfo]>, Arc<OperationError>>` backed by `SchemaCatalog::refresh_columns`. It shares an in-flight fetch, commits the new list over the cached one on success, keeps the cached list and sets last_error on failure, and never clears the entry. W5-11 uses it for Retry and after committed Save(SchemaChanges); W5-12 uses it for browse Refresh and Retry. A catalog test asserts a failed refresh returns the error while `columns(table)` still returns the old list.
- XW15-count-big (W3 browse build_count owner, W2 mssql driver): `browse::build_count` emits `SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) ...` for the SQL Server dialect, avoiding Msg 8115 above 2,147,483,647 rows; other engines keep COUNT(*), whose results are 64-bit. Every driver's `count_rows` decodes non-negative Int, UInt or WideInt into u64 and returns DriverError::Decode otherwise. Tests: a dialect snapshot test for the SQL Server COUNT_BIG text and an mssql integration test that count_rows returns a u64.

### W6 · SQL editor, history and dialogs

Revised W6 plan: 23 commit-sized tasks in dependency order that fix all 16 owned findings and resolve every review point.

Review resolutions:
- PG scripts: the editor sends one statement per EditorSession::run for every semicolon engine, as psql, mysql, sqlite3 and clickhouse-client do. T-SQL sends one GO batch per run. No implicit multi-statement transaction exists, so completed Command entries are true. `VACUUM; SELECT 1;` behaves as in psql, and history sums are exact.
- History at the switch: `HistoryService::store()` now arrives in W6-10 (pre-switch, after step 21), before W6-12 records history with it.
- Step-25 layout: W6-12 and W6-13 edit `ui/app/*`. The dialog emits `ConnectSubmission { request, pending_save }` to the pre-FA-11 App. There is deliberately no step-28 dialog change: SessionKey is window routing that FA 11 derives from `pending_save.connection.id`.
- ScriptExecution: removed from `ScriptPlan::build`. The execution unit comes from `ScriptSyntax.statement_boundary`, and W6 never reads `DriverCapabilities.script_execution`.
- Contract amendments: exactly two, requested with exact signatures (`DriverCapabilities.script`, `EditorSession::lexical_settings`). Session::capabilities, driver_display_name and catalog are not needed. A `WorkspaceIdentity { engine: EngineProfile, connection_id, connection_name }` is built from the verified `ConnectRequest.driver`, and data comes from the existing Session::objects/columns.
- F-027: the markup boundary covers every sink found by grep, including connection_row.rs, browse_tab.rs:1355, PreferencesGroup (use-markup=True in its .ui with no property to disable it), ComboRow use-subtitle, Banner and TabPage tooltip. A clippy ban lists every markup-parsing setter and builder; each path was checked in libadwaita 0.9.1 and gtk4 0.11.2 sources, and clippy's own test config shows trait-method and re-export paths resolve.
- Format re-lexes sqlformat output with ScriptLexer and copies a statement verbatim when its significant tokens change. `uppercase: None`, because sqlformat's keyword list uppercases STATUS and LEVEL (tokenizer.rs:981,1140), which are case-sensitive identifiers in ClickHouse.
- Results use AdwOverlaySplitView with a toolbar toggle bound to show-sidebar, so no back navigation is needed.
- Compound tracking follows psqlscan.l (CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION/PROCEDURE, paren depth, BEGIN/CASE/END) and sqlite3_complete (CREATE TRIGGER ends at `;END;`). MySQL gets none, as the mysql client and MySQL manual require DELIMITER. SQLite brackets have no `]]` doubling. ANSI_QUOTES is not modelled; this matches the mysql client, which honours only SERVER_STATUS_NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.
- Minor fixes:
  - The Enter test emits activate on the row's delegate GtkText; adw-entry-row.c calls gtk_widget_activate_default from that handler.
  - Fuzzy matching goes through `sourceview5::ffi` with `glib::casefold`.
  - History schema uses PRAGMA user_version gating.
  - Retention applies on the existing hourly prune.
  - confirm-destructive is removed inside FD 12's commit.
  - Keyring tests are pure.
  - The connect dialog keeps typed fields across driver switches and reads the port from `caps.endpoint`.
  - Run-state edge cases (Opening, Failed, Busy, diagnostics, Lost) are specified.

Order:
- Pre-switch: W6-01 (inside step 17), W6-02 to W6-10.
- Inside the step-25 switch: W6-11 to W6-13.
- Post-switch: W6-14 to W6-23.

Root cause: libadwaita parses Toast title, Banner title, StatusPage description, PreferencesRow title and subtitles (including ComboRow use-subtitle, per adw-combo-row.c), PreferencesGroup title and description (use-markup=True in adw-preferences-group.ui) and TabPage tooltip as Pango markup. Data and translations both reach these properties.

`plain_text.rs` is the only module allowed to call those setters. Each fn carries `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods, reason = "markup-safe boundary")]`:
- `toast(&str) -> adw::Toast` and `timed_toast(&str, u32)` use `.use_markup(false)`.
- `banner(&str) -> adw::Banner` and `set_banner_title` use `use_markup(false)`.
- `set_status_description(&adw::StatusPage, &str)` escapes with `glib::markup_escape_text`; StatusPage has no use-markup.
- Row setters `set_row_title(&impl IsA<adw::PreferencesRow>, &str)`, `set_row_subtitle(&impl IsA<adw::ActionRow>, &str)` and `set_expander_subtitle` call `set_use_markup(false)` first.
- Row builder constructors seeded with `.use_markup(false).title(title)`: `action_row(title, subtitle: Option<&str>)`, `expander_row`, `switch_row`, `combo_row`, `spin_row`, `entry_row(title)`, `password_entry_row`, `button_row`.
- `group(title, description: Option<&str>) -> PreferencesGroupBuilder` and `set_group_description` escape, because the group has no use-markup.
- `set_tab_tooltip(&adw::TabPage, &str)` escapes. Every tab sets it, so the tooltip never falls back to the title.

Call sites converted:
- Every row in the listed files, including `connection_row.rs:45-46` (saved name and user@host).
- Every toast (connect_dialog.rs:571, status_pages.rs:35,55, app/mod.rs:1315, export_dialog.rs:267).
- Every StatusPage description (outcome view, timeout reason, structure_tab/mod.rs:851, browse_tab.rs:1290,1303,1355, whose loading page embeds the table name).
- Banners (browse_tab.rs:1385-1390, app/mod.rs:687).
- Groups, and tab titles in workspace_tabs.rs and structure.rs.
- Manual `markup_escape_text` in columns.rs, fks.rs and indexes.rs is replaced by the row helpers.
- Structure `LoadFailed` always sets the description.

AdwWindowTitle and AdwAlertDialog heading/body are plain by default (adw-window-title.ui has no use-markup) and stay unchanged.

#### W6-05 · Add a data-driven SQL script lexer and planner to core

**Step**: 5 · **Findings**: F-030  
**Depends on**: W8-02  
**Contracts**: FD-D8  
**Commit**: `feat(core): add a dialect-driven SQL script lexer and planner`

**Files**: `crates/core/src/script/mod.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/script_syntax.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/string_quote.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/identifier_quote.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/line_comment_prefix.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/compound_rule.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/lexical_settings.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/token.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/lexer.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/compound_tracker.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/script_plan.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/script_batch.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/statement_span.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/script_diagnostic.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/script/text_offsets.rs (new)`, `crates/core/src/lib.rs`

Engine-agnostic mechanism, driven only by data. No dependency on DriverCapabilities, so it compiles at step 4.

`ScriptSyntax` fields:
- `string_quotes: &'static [StringQuote { quote, doubled, backslash: BackslashEscape { Never, Always, WhenEnabled } }]`
- `identifier_quotes: &'static [IdentifierQuote { open, close, doubled_close: bool }]`
- `line_comments: &'static [LineCommentPrefix { text, requires_following_whitespace }]`
- `block_comments: BlockComments { Flat, Nested }`
- `dollar_quotes: bool`, `escape_string_prefixes: &'static [char]`
- `statement_boundary: StatementBoundary { Semicolon, GoBatch }`
- `compound_rule: CompoundRule { None, RoutineBody, TriggerBody }`
- `parentheses_hold_terminator: bool`, `delimiter_directive: bool`
- `batch_error: BatchErrorPolicy { StopScript, ContinueNextBatch }`
- `default_lexical: LexicalSettings`, `keywords: &'static [&'static str]`

`LexicalSettings { backslash_escapes: bool }`.

Lexer: `ScriptLexer<'a>: Iterator<Item = ScriptToken { kind, range }>`. TokenKind is { Whitespace, LineComment, BlockComment, StringLiteral, QuotedIdentifier, DollarQuoted, Word, Semicolon, OpenParen, CloseParen, CustomDelimiter, DelimiterDirective { delimiter }, GoSeparator { repeat: NonZeroU32 }, Punct, Unterminated(OpenConstruct) }.

Lexing rules:
- Dollar tags are `$`, `$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, not preceded by an identifier char or `$`.
- E/e prefixes always allow backslash escapes.
- `WhenEnabled` follows LexicalSettings.
- `requires_following_whitespace` covers MySQL `-- ` and ClickHouse `# `.
- Nested comments track depth.
- GO is a line whose trimmed text outside any construct is `GO` [positive int] [-- comment], case-insensitive; `GO;` is not a separator.
- DELIMITER or `\d` lines are recognised at statement start and line start.

Compound rules (only in these reference contexts):
- `RoutineBody` follows psqlscan.l. Only when the statement's leading words are CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION|PROCEDURE, and only at paren depth 0: BEGIN adds 1, CASE adds 1 when depth is at least 1, END subtracts 1 when depth is positive. So `SELECT begin FROM t; SELECT 2;` and `BEGIN; UPDATE..; COMMIT;` split normally.
- `TriggerBody` follows sqlite3_complete. A statement starting [EXPLAIN] CREATE [TEMP|TEMPORARY] TRIGGER ends only at a `;` whose two preceding significant tokens are `;` then END.
- `parentheses_hold_terminator` follows psql: a `;` at paren depth above 0 never terminates (CREATE RULE ... DO ALSO (INSERT ..; UPDATE ..)).

Plan API: `ScriptPlan::build(text: &str, base: usize, syntax: &ScriptSyntax, settings: LexicalSettings) -> ScriptPlan` with `batches()`, `statements()`, `statement_at(byte)` and `diagnostics()`.
- `ScriptBatch { range, repeat: NonZeroU32 }`.
- `StatementSpan { range (no terminator or trivia), extent (through its terminator and same-line trailing trivia) }`.
- The execution unit comes from `statement_boundary`, following each engine's own CLI:
  - Semicolon: one batch per statement. Custom-delimiter statements have the delimiter stripped; directive lines belong to no batch.
  - GoBatch: one batch per GO region with its repeat count, and `statements()` equals the batches.
- `ScriptDiagnostic::Unterminated { construct, start }`.
- `text_offsets::{char_to_byte, byte_to_char}` convert GtkTextIter offsets.

Linear time, no per-token allocation.

**Tests**: Fixture-syntax unit tests:
- `dollar_quoted_body_hides_semicolons`
- `tagged_dollar_quote_with_inner_double_dollar`
- `identifier_with_dollar_is_not_a_quote`
- `escape_string_backslash_quote`
- `backslash_escape_when_enabled_vs_disabled`
- `nested_block_comment`
- `routine_begin_atomic_block_is_one_statement`
- `routine_case_end_inside_body`
- `begin_column_outside_routine_is_identifier`
- `transaction_begin_is_not_a_block`
- `parenthesised_rule_actions_are_one_statement`
- `trigger_body_ends_at_semicolon_end_semicolon`
- `trigger_case_end_inside_body`
- `delimiter_directive_splits_procedure` (exact byte ranges)
- `go_count_repeats_batch`
- `go_semicolon_is_not_separator`
- `go_inside_string_is_not_separator`
- `double_dash_needs_whitespace` (`SELECT 1--1`)
- `bracket_without_doubling_ends_at_first_close`

#### W6-06 · Declare each engine's script syntax and completion keywords

**Step**: 6 · **Findings**: F-030, F-090  
**Depends on**: W6-05  
**Contracts**: DRIVER  
**Commit**: `feat(drivers): declare script lexing rules and keywords per engine`

**Files**: `crates/drivers/postgres/src/script_syntax.rs (new)`, `crates/drivers/mysql/src/script_syntax.rs (new)`, `crates/drivers/sqlite/src/script_syntax.rs (new)`, `crates/drivers/mssql/src/script_syntax.rs (new)`, `crates/drivers/clickhouse/src/script_syntax.rs (new)`, `crates/drivers/postgres/src/lib.rs`, `crates/drivers/mysql/src/lib.rs`, `crates/drivers/sqlite/src/lib.rs`, `crates/drivers/mssql/src/lib.rs`, `crates/drivers/clickhouse/src/lib.rs`

Each driver exports `pub const SCRIPT_SYNTAX: ScriptSyntax`:

| Engine | Strings | Identifiers | Comments | Compound and parens | Boundary, batch error | default_lexical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL | `'` doubled, WhenEnabled; E prefix; dollar quotes | `"` doubled | `--`, Nested | RoutineBody, parens hold | Semicolon, StopScript | backslash false (standard_conforming_strings on) |
| MySQL/MariaDB | `'` and `"` doubled, WhenEnabled | backtick doubled | `-- ` needs whitespace, `#`, Flat | None, DELIMITER directive | Semicolon, StopScript | backslash true |
| SQLite | `'` doubled | `"`, backtick, `[..]` without doubling | `--`, Flat | TriggerBody | Semicolon, StopScript | false |
| SQL Server | `'` doubled | `[..]` with `]]`, `"` | `--`, Nested | None | GoBatch, ContinueNextBatch (sqlcmd/SSMS) | false |
| ClickHouse | `'` doubled, Always backslash; heredoc | backtick, `"` | `--`, `#!`, `# `, `//`, Nested | None | Semicolon, StopScript | true |

Review points answered:
- MySQL gets no BEGIN tracking. The mysql client splits at the delimiter and the MySQL manual (stored-programs-defining) requires DELIMITER for BEGIN…END bodies. Tracking would also misread the non-reserved `begin` in `SET NEW.begin = 1`, and `XA BEGIN`.
- ANSI_QUOTES is not modelled. mysql's add_line treats `"` as a quote and consults only SERVER_STATUS_NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, so a script that runs in mysql splits identically here.

`keywords` holds each engine's reserved and common words.

The constants reach DriverCapabilities through the DRIVER amendment inside the switch (cross_workstream_needs).

**Tests**: Per-crate `cargo test --lib`:
- postgres: `plpgsql_function_and_do_block_plan`, `begin_atomic_function_is_one_statement`, `begin_column_select_splits`.
- mysql: `procedure_with_delimiter_plans_three_batches`, `procedure_without_delimiter_splits_like_mysql_client`, `xa_begin_is_a_plain_statement`, `hash_comment_hides_semicolon`, `backtick_identifier_with_semicolon`.
- sqlite: `create_trigger_with_case_end_is_one_statement`, `bracket_identifier_has_no_doubling`.
- mssql: `go_lines_split_batches_and_statement_at_returns_batch`, `bracket_identifier_closing_doubled`.
- clickhouse: `heredoc_hides_semicolon`, `slash_comment`.
- Every crate: `keywords_are_uppercase_ascii_and_unique`.

**Step**: 30 · **Findings**: F-029, F-030, F-092

This is W6's slice of the step-25 switch, grounded in the step-25 layout (`ui/app/workspace_tabs.rs`). The editor loses `database_service::instance()`, `conn.query` and the client-side timeout race.

**Identity.**
- `EngineProfile { driver_id, display_name, capabilities: &'static DriverCapabilities }` with `EngineProfile::of(&dyn DatabaseDriver)` (DRIVER id, display_name and capabilities verified).
- `WorkspaceIdentity { engine: EngineProfile, connection_id: Uuid, connection_name: String }`, set on App by the connect consumer (W6-13) and by `on_open_saved` from the SavedConnection plus the registry driver.
- No Session::capabilities or Session::catalog amendment is needed.

**Init.** `SqlEditorInit { session: Arc<Session>, identity: WorkspaceIdentity, settings: AppSettings, history: HistoryService, spawner: Arc<dyn TaskSpawner>, initial_query: Option<String> }`. `schema_words` takes `&[ObjectInfo]`, because TableInfo is deleted; W6-17 removes the file.

**Slot.** `EditorSessionSlot { state: Opening | Ready(Arc<dyn EditorSession>) | Lost | Failed(OperationError), generation }`, opened by a GuardedCommand calling `session.open_editor_session(EditorSessionOptions { statement_timeout }, &cancel)`.
- Opening: Run is insensitive with tooltip "Opening a connection for this editor…" and the status bar shows an adw::Spinner.
- Failed: `adw::Banner` (plain_text) with the operation message and button "Retry", which reopens.
- Lost: Banner "This editor's connection was lost." with button "Reconnect", which reopens.

**Scope.** `RunScope::resolve(has_selection, selection, cursor)`:
- Run uses a non-empty `selection_bounds()`, else the whole buffer.
- RunAtCursor uses `ScriptPlan::statement_at`.
- `connect_has_selection_notify` switches the label between Run Selection and Run, with matching tooltips.

**Plan and execution unit.** `RunRequest { text, base_char, plan }` from `ScriptPlan::build(scoped, base, identity.engine.capabilities.script, editor_session.lexical_settings().unwrap_or(script.default_lexical))`.
- `script_runner.rs` sends each `ScriptBatch` in its own `editor_session.run(UserSql, RunOptions { row_limit: RowLimit::EDITOR_DEFAULT, deadline: query_timeout (0 means None), cancel: run_token.child_token() }, Box::new(ChannelResultSink))`, `repeat` times.
- Semicolon engines send exactly one statement per run, as psql, mysql, sqlite3 and clickhouse-client do. No multi-statement text reaches PostgreSQL, so there is no implicit transaction that could roll back earlier statements, VACUUM and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY run as in psql, and Command entries report only what the server committed or holds in an explicit transaction.
- SQL Server sends each GO batch whole; a T-SQL batch has no implicit transaction.
- After each run, if `lexical_settings()` changed, the unexecuted remainder is re-planned (psql re-reads standard_conforming_strings the same way).
- On `RunEnd::Failed` the script stops unless `batch_error == ContinueNextBatch`, and the remaining batches become NotRun.

**Errors.**
- `Err(EditorSessionBusy)` becomes a Failed entry with the W6-11 message; the batch is not retried.
- `Err` of category ConnectionLost sets the slot to Lost and calls `session.signal(MonitorSignal::ProbeRequested { generation })`.
- An Unterminated diagnostic adds a `ClientWarning` entry ("Unterminated dollar-quoted string starting on line 12") and the text is still sent, so the server reports the error.
- Stop and Escape cancel run_token.

**Sink.** `ChannelResultSink` sends `BatchEvent` over `async_channel::bounded(8)` and returns `SinkFlow::ConsumerGone` on send error. The GTK side drains it with `glib::spawn_future_local` into `RunLog`, a pure state machine producing `RunLogEntry` { ResultSet { columns, retained, total, truncation, batch }, Command { rows_affected, batch }, Notice, Failed { error, batch }, ClientWarning, Cancelled, TimedOut { server_cancelled }, NotRun { batch } }. Command titles read "{n} rows affected".

**Results pane.**
- `adw::BreakpointBin` (width_request 360, height_request 180) holds an `adw::ToolbarView`.
- Top bar (run_status): a `gtk::ToggleButton` `sidebar-show-symbolic` "Show Results List", an `adw::Spinner`, an ngettext summary, and a transaction label ("Transaction open", or "Transaction failed, roll back to continue").
- Content: `adw::OverlaySplitView`.
  - Sidebar: `gtk::ScrolledWindow` with a `gtk::ListView` (`navigation-sidebar`) over `gio::ListStore<ResultItem>`, `SingleSelection` and `SignalListItemFactory` rows (icon, title such as "Result 2 · 1,204 rows", dim batch preview).
  - Content: a `gtk::Stack` of per-entry widgets.
- `adw::Breakpoint` `max-width: 560sp` sets collapsed=true.
- The toggle's `active` is bound bidirectionally to `show-sidebar`, so a collapsed sidebar is always reachable with no back navigation. Selecting an entry while collapsed calls `set_show_sidebar(false)`.
- Pure `SidebarPolicy::decide(entries, collapsed, previous) -> SidebarState { toggle_visible, show_sidebar }`: 0 or 1 entries hide the toggle and the sidebar; going to 2 while expanded shows it; collapsed leaves it to the user.
- The first Failed entry is selected, else the first entry.

**Result widgets.**
- ResultSet uses W5's streaming grid, with a dim truncation label.
- Failed uses a StatusPage via `plain_text::set_status_description`, plus a "Go to Error" pill when `ServerDiagnostics.position` exists; the cursor goes to base_char + batch start + position - 1.

**Transaction dirty.** Pure `transaction_dirty(slot, last_state, has_run)` is false for Opening, Lost and Failed; true for InTransaction or Failed; and for Unknown equals has_run. Changes emit `SqlEditorOutput::OpenTransactionChanged(bool)`, which workspace_tabs.rs stores on the editor slot for FA 10's DirtyKind.

**History.** `run_history.rs` records one `NewEntry` per Run through `history.store()` (W6-10) on the spawner:
- query: the executed scoped text;
- outcome: first failure, else Cancelled, else Success;
- rows_affected: the sum of Command counts, else retained rows;
- connection fields from WorkspaceIdentity.

**APIs**: core EditorSession::run, RunOptions, ResultSink, ResultEvent, RunSummary, TransactionState (EDITOR); tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken::child_token; async_channel::bounded (2.5); gtk::TextBuffer::selection_bounds/connect_has_selection_notify; adw::BreakpointBin, adw::Breakpoint, adw::BreakpointCondition::parse (1.4); adw::OverlaySplitView::set_collapsed/set_show_sidebar/connect_show_sidebar_notify (1.4, crate 0.9.1); adw::ToolbarView::add_top_bar; glib::ObjectExt::bind_property(..).bidirectional().sync_create(); gtk::ListView, SignalListItemFactory, SingleSelection, gio::ListStore, gtk::Stack; adw::Spinner (1.6); adw::Banner::set_button_label/connect_button_clicked (1.3); glib::spawn_future_local

#### W6-14 · Format only statements whose tokens survive sqlformat

**Step**: 31 · **Findings**: F-028  
**Depends on**: W6-12  
**Commit**: `fix(editor): keep statements sqlformat would change unformatted`

**Files**: `crates/app/src/ui/editor/format_plan.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/editor/significant_tokens.rs (new)`, `crates/app/src/ui/editor/mod.rs`

`format_script(text, syntax, settings, dialect: sqlformat::Dialect) -> String`:
1. Build the ScriptPlan.
2. For each statement range, run `sqlformat::format` with `FormatOptions { indent: Spaces(4), uppercase: None, lines_between_queries: 1, dialect }`.
3. Accept the output only if `significant_tokens(output) == significant_tokens(input)` under the same ScriptLexer. Tokens are compared as (kind, exact text), Whitespace is ignored, and comment text is compared with trailing whitespace trimmed.
4. Otherwise copy the statement verbatim.

This one rule covers what sqlformat 0.5.0 cannot lex (tokenizer.rs:189-250):
- `//` and `#!` comments;
- nested block comments, which end at the first `*/`;
- backslash always escaping inside `'` and `"` (wrong for standard_conforming_strings and SQLite);
- `--1` read as a comment in MySQL;
- `$$` read as a keyword;
- `[..]` outside Dialect::SQLServer.

It also covers statements containing DollarQuoted, directive, GO or Unterminated tokens.

`uppercase: None`, because sqlformat's reserved list uppercases STATUS and LEVEL (tokenizer.rs:981,1140), which are case-sensitive identifiers in ClickHouse and in MySQL table names on Linux.

Inter-statement trivia, terminators, GO lines and DELIMITER lines are preserved byte for byte. The dialect comes from ScriptSyntax: dollar_quotes plus E prefix gives PostgreSql, Bracket-with-doubling gives SQLServer, otherwise Generic.

Format uses `identity.engine.capabilities.script` with `replace_all_undoable` and `CursorAnchor`.

**APIs**: sqlformat::format, FormatOptions { uppercase, dialect } (sqlformat 0.5.0); gtk::TextBuffer user actions

**Tests**: - `dollar_tag_body_is_untouched`
- `clickhouse_slash_comment_statement_kept_verbatim` (`SELECT 1 // note`)
- `nested_block_comment_kept_verbatim`
- `standard_conforming_backslash_string_kept_verbatim` (`SELECT 'C:\' AS a, 'x'`)
- `mysql_minus_minus_arithmetic_kept_verbatim`
- `go_lines_preserved`
- `delimiter_procedure_preserved`
- `plain_select_is_reflowed_case_preserved`
- `format_is_idempotent_for_plain_statements`
